# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect full from #3375, #3380 (batch pass)

Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #3419

## Current State

Path-guard discipline is a written rule with no mechanical home. `docs/donts.md` carries [IL-150] (resolve a leaf symlink, fail closed on an unprovable leaf) and [IL-161] (an existence check is not a type check — lstat first). IL-161's own removal condition names the fix: "a shared lstat-backed helper new filesystem-check code is required to route through". No such helper exists and no record tracks it.

Multi-spec run 2026-10-17T144508-spec-3375-3380 broke the rule three more times in two new readers, each caught only at review:

- #3375 `plugin/bin/lib/timing/transcript.js`: a symlinked `subagents/` directory was realpathed and read (ledger row 20, fixed in 759b89a29), and an lstat failure fell through to the symlink-following read path, which fails open (row 24, fixed in 4cb8e74ac).
- #3380 `plugin/bin/lib/superpowers-version.js` / `installed-plugins.js`: the home exclusion and the ancestor match compared `fs.realpathSync` output, which echoes input casing, so a mis-cased path on a case-insensitive volume slipped past the guard (row 48, fixed in 722ece0d6 by switching to `fs.realpathSync.native`).

Each reader hand-rolls its own lstat / realpath / containment logic: `transcript.js` locateTranscripts and readDispatches, `installed-plugins.js` safeRealpath, and `realTarget()` inside `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`. Nothing lets a new reader reuse the hardened form.

## Deliverables

- A shared module under `plugin/bin/lib/` (a flat sibling directory, per CLAUDE.md's structure note) that exposes the hardened primitives:
  - an lstat-backed type check (file / directory / symlink / missing);
  - leaf-symlink resolution that fails closed on a dangling or unreadable leaf;
  - a case-canonical realpath (`fs.realpathSync.native`);
  - an ancestor-or-self containment test built on those three.

- `transcript.js`, `installed-plugins.js` and `pre-tool-use.js`'s `realTarget()` routed through it, with no behavior change. Their existing tests stay green unmodified.

- A conformance test or lint over `plugin/bin/**/*.js` that flags a new bare `fs.realpathSync(` / `existsSync`-as-type-check call outside the shared module, with an explicit allowlist for each existing caller that is judged safe.

- [IL-150] and [IL-161] updated to point at the helper, and their removal conditions applied (retire or narrow them).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each primitive has unit tests for the symlinked-leaf, dangling-leaf, lstat-failure and mis-cased-path inputs. Each test is shown red against a naive `fs.realpathSync` / `existsSync` stand-in.

- [ ] All three named call sites import the shared module, and `npm test` passes with their existing suites unchanged.

- [ ] The lint/conformance test fails when a fixture adds a bare `fs.realpathSync(` call in a new `plugin/bin/lib/` file, and passes on the current tree.

- [ ] `docs/donts.md`'s [IL-150]/[IL-161] lines name the helper, and `docs/incident-log.md` records which removal condition was met.

## Release Note

Internal hardening: plugin filesystem readers share one symlink- and case-safe path helper.

`/claude-tweaks:build`'s plan-authoring checks (`plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`) have no rule for deriving a "every reader of X" inventory. Record #3358's plan derived its marker-reader inventory from greps for marker literals (`<!-- `, `## Verification Brief`, named marker prefixes). It missed six readers that match on plain sentences or on prefixes the greps never named: `tidy/SKILL.md`'s parent-gate re-query, `release/bookkeeping.md`'s `Shipped in v…` check, `_shared/headless-self-report.md`'s `Resolved build:` check, the retry-marker prose callers, and `health-core/materiality-digest.js`. ## Deliverables

When a spec's deliverables say to apply something "at every reader of" a value (comments, markers, labels, files), the plan derives the inventory from the read call sites (`--json comments`, `/comments` REST paths, `issue_read`/`get_comments`, `.comments[]`, `listComments`, and so on), then classifies each hit. Greps for the value's literal text are a supplement, never the source.

2. Cite #3358's six missed readers as the motivating example, in one sentence.

Origin: /claude-tweaks:build #3365 Common Step 4 (whole-branch review, declined-to-judge)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#3365 made Review Console step 11 (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md`) always record an `issues` array via `set-verify-expectations.js --issues` on its non-Approve-all path, because wrap-up verify runs after cleanup — by then the worktree mirror holding the materialized header is gone under pr-first, and the main checkout has no `work/` until reconcile.

The Approve-all path instead runs `wrap-up-engine.js finish-console --approve-all`, whose step 1 (`plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js`, the `writeExpectations({ runDir, fields: { memory, upstream } })` call) writes only `memory`/`upstream`. On a pr-first Approve-all run `engine-verify.js`'s `resolvedIssueNumbers` therefore finds no header and no expectations `issues`, and the `carrier-commit` check reports `skip` instead of pass/fail — the silent skip #3365 set out to remove.

## Deliverables

1. `finish-console` accepts an optional `issues` array in its stdin payload (validated as positive integers in `validateFinishConsolePayload`) and writes it through `writeExpectations` alongside `memory`/`upstream`.

2. `review-console.md` step 11's Approve-all sentence includes `issues` in the payload, sourced exactly as the non-Approve-all path sources it (`wrap-up-pack.json`'s `inputs.records` only when `sources.records` is `headers` or `worktree-headers`, else Phase 1's record; omitted when no record resolves).

3. Tests: a `finish-console` CLI case for the new key, and the step-11 prose pin in `tests/wrap-up-record-resolution-conformance.test.js` extended to the Approve-all sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `finish-console --approve-all` payload carrying `issues: [N]` leaves `verify-expectations.json` with `issues: [N]`, preserving every other field.

2. A payload with a non-integer `issues` entry is rejected with a validation error (exit 1), writing nothing.

3. On a fixture run dir with no header anywhere and that expectations file, `runVerify`'s `carrier-commit` row resolves `N` (pass or fail), never `skip`.

4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Wrap-up verification now checks the closing keyword on runs approved with "Approve all", instead of silently skipping it.

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

Part of the "Build dispatch cost shape" decomposition (origin #3229, a feedback report from a measured 10-task subagent-driven build). In that build, 3 of the 5 Important findings from the top-tier final review were spec or plan-level gaps — behaviour the spec left undecided, or two tasks disagreeing about a contract — found after all the code was written and fixed in an 18-minute fix wave plus a re-review. SDD's own pre-flight scan ("Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts") runs on the controller and hunts contradictions between and within tasks; it does not look for spec gaps or undecided behaviour.

This record adds a new `/build` Common Step between plan audit (Common Step 1.5) and execution dispatch (Common Step 2), Spec Mode only: one dispatched reviewer on the Capable profile reads the materialized spec and the plan once and returns findings in three classes — spec gap (the spec does not decide something the plan must decide), undecided behaviour (an input class, failure mode or UI state no task covers) and cross-task contract (one task produces what another consumes and they disagree). It explicitly does not redo SDD's pre-flight conflict table. A spec gap resolvable from the spec's own intent amends the in-run materialized spec before Task 1; a spec gap that needs a human becomes a deliberate new HARD-GATE stop; the other two classes amend the plan.

**Complexity:** Medium-High
**Estimated tasks:** 6-8

## Non-Goals

- Redoing SDD's pre-flight conflict table (cross-task and within-task contradictions, written to the SDD ledger). The reviewer's brief tells it to skip that class.
- Editing the live issue body at any point. An intent-resolvable spec amendment lives in the worktree's materialized spec and is posted once as a comment on the record; nothing is staged for the Review Console.
- Running in design mode (no materialized spec, no record) — same skip as architecture alignment.
- Changing SDD's per-task loop, or filing anything upstream with superpowers.
- The per-task tier markers (a separate record, which adds one check to this record's reviewer once both exist).

## Prerequisites

| Record | Title | Status |
|--------|-------|--------|
| #3375 | Attribute agent cost to individual subagent dispatches in phase-timing and the /wrap-up run summary | must ship first, so the plan reviewer's own cost and the final-review finding classes it is meant to reduce are measurable |
| #3376 | Re-pin superpowers to 7.0.0 and pin the upstream text the dispatch cost-shape changes lean on | must ship first, so the SDD pre-flight sentence this step is defined against is pinned |
| #3310 | Cut every skill-size consumer over to the rail, load delta, and size outlier | ready, in progress — shares `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`, `plan-audit.md`, `plan-authoring-checks.md`, `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`; build after it merges |

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — `### Common Step 1.5: Plan Audit`, then `### Common Step 1.7: Design Pre-Build (frontend specs + terminal)`, then `### Common Step 2: Execute the Plan`. The file is 45,995 bytes against the shared 51,200-byte ceiling, so the new step must be a short pointer to a new sub-file (measured 2026-10-17).
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` and `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — the mechanical plan audit (Checks A-E plus headroom) that Step 1.5 runs; Check E (warn-only) already compares the materialized spec's Acceptance Criteria clauses to the plan.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the dispatch contract (minimal input, trailing `STATUS:` line, inlined output template, model profile selection); Template A (a findings table) lives in `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Template A section.
- `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js` — resolves `capable` to a model; dispatch sites call it and pass the model explicitly.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — the canonical entry schema for `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/decisions.md`.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — the "What `auto` never silences" table; its HARD-GATE / BLOCKED / STOP row (around line 208) names `/build` Design Step 3 plan validation and Common Step 1.5 plan-audit hard-fails, and has no entry for a step between 1.5 and 2.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` — the single roster of what each `ceremony-profile` skips, pinned by `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`.
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — the materialized spec (`work/{n}-spec.md`) lives in the worktree's copy in worktree mode, not under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, and reaches the main checkout only on merge.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — how `/dispatch` blocks a record today: a `gh issue comment` attempt comment, then `bot:blocked` added (and every `auto:*` grant removed) with a `PushNotification`. `plugin/skills/_shared/headless-self-report.md` and `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1` are the existing "no human present" signals.
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — the `## build` section is where any new `/build` edge is stated, once.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A new sub-file in `plugin/skills/build/` (the builder names it; `plan-review.md` suggested) holding the full procedure: skip conditions, the dispatch prompt with the inlined output template, the three finding classes, and the per-class handling below.
- [ ] A short new Common Step in `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` between 1.5 and 2 that states the Spec-Mode-only condition and points at the sub-file (pointer only; no procedure restated in `SKILL.md`).
- [ ] The dispatch: one reviewer on Capable, model resolved through `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/resolve-profile.js" capable --run-dir "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR"`, under the Subagent Contract. Input is the materialized spec path and plan path only (no conversation history); the reviewer may also read the repository read-only to check what the plan integrates with, because undecided-behaviour and cross-task findings depend on existing code; trailing `STATUS:` line; output template inlined verbatim in the prompt.
- [ ] The output template carries, for each spec-gap finding, a `Resolution` field (`intent-resolvable` or `needs-human`) and the spec sentence that supports an `intent-resolvable` call. Burden of proof: when no spec sentence can be cited, the finding is `needs-human`. A gap is `needs-human` whenever it would alter or loosen an existing Acceptance Criterion or an observable contract, or has two defensible readings. An undecided-behaviour finding that is really a product decision is reclassified by the reviewer as a spec gap.
- [ ] The class boundary against SDD's pre-flight scan is written into the brief: the pre-flight scan checks plan-internal contradictions (a task against the plan's Global Constraints, a step the plan mandates that the review rubric forbids); this reviewer checks producer/consumer agreement between tasks (names, shapes, ordering of what one task produces and another consumes) and each against the spec. The brief gives one example of each.
- [ ] Handling for a spec gap marked `intent-resolvable`: amend the worktree's copy of `work/{n}-spec.md` before Task 1 with an additive clarification only (never editing or loosening an existing Acceptance Criterion), commit the amendment in the worktree together with any plan amendment, write the decision log entry per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`, and post the amendment as one comment on the record (`gh issue comment`, or the MCP equivalent per `_shared/github-write-transport.md`) so the record's history carries it. The record body is never edited and nothing is staged for the Review Console: the amended in-run spec is the one `/test`, `/review` and `/wrap-up` judge against, so there is no staged item to apply, decline, or leave unreached.
- [ ] Handling for undecided-behaviour and cross-task-contract findings: amend the plan file, log it, and proceed. After any spec or plan amendment, re-run `plan-audit.js` once on the amended plan (Checks A, C, D, headroom, and E against the amended spec); the plan review itself does not re-run, so the step cannot loop.
- [ ] Standalone `/build` (no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, no `config.yml`): the step still runs and amends the spec; the decision-log write is skipped and the amendment is listed in the Step 7 handoff (the record comment is still posted) (the same standalone fallback `plan-audit.md` and `SKILL.md` use for their own run-directory-anchored parts).
- [ ] A new HARD-GATE row in `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` for a spec gap marked `needs-human`: a real stop before Task 1 in every mode when someone is present; when nobody is (`DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1`, the existing headless marker `/dispatch` sets for a scheduled Routine drain), the record goes `bot:blocked` with the question posted on it, through the transport `/dispatch` already uses for blocked records (issue comment, `bot:blocked`, every `auto:*` grant removed). The row names the exit state: the claim is released, the worktree and draft PR are left in place, nothing is merged, and the run reports `BLOCKED` with the question to its caller; a human answers on the record, re-grants `auto:build` at `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`, and the next dispatch re-materializes from the answered record.
- [ ] The same HARD-GATE enumeration is updated at every consumer that restates it: `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` (line 36 lists the same gate families) and any other file a repo-wide grep for the existing row's wording finds, with a conformance assertion that each named consumer cites the new gate.
- [ ] The skip conditions: `ceremony-profile: fast-lane` (a new roster row with a new tag in `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md`), and a trivial plan (the builder picks and documents the threshold, reusing an existing triviality signal such as Step 1.5's fewer-than-3-file-references condition where it fits). A skip writes a `SKIP` entry per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s degrade-trace rule.
- [ ] The reviewer's brief tells it explicitly not to repeat SDD's pre-flight conflict table.
- [ ] Any new `/build` edge added to `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `## build` section (for example to `/dispatch` for the blocked-record transport).
- [ ] Tests: a conformance suite pinning the new step's placement and pointer, the roster row, and the HARD-GATE row; plus byte-ceiling checks for every grown file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` contains a Common Step positioned after `Common Step 1.5: Plan Audit` and before `Common Step 2: Execute the Plan` that names Spec Mode only and points at the new sub-file, and the file stays under 51,200 bytes (and under any tighter per-skill pin found by the Byte-pin check).
2. The new sub-file states the three finding classes by name (spec gap, undecided behaviour, cross-task contract), states that SDD's pre-flight conflict table is not redone, and inlines the output template and a trailing `STATUS:` requirement verbatim in the dispatch prompt text.
3. The sub-file's dispatch resolves the model with `resolve-profile.js capable` and passes the resolved model explicitly; no model name is hardcoded.
4. For an `intent-resolvable` spec-gap finding the sub-file prescribes, in order: amend the worktree's `work/{n}-spec.md` additively (never editing or loosening an existing Acceptance Criterion), commit it, log the decision, post the amendment as one comment on the record, and re-run `plan-audit.js` once; and states that no `gh issue edit` runs against the live record and nothing is staged for the Review Console. The sub-file states the standalone-`/build` fallback (amendment listed in the Step 7 handoff, no decision-log write).
5. `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s HARD-GATE row names this step's `needs-human` spec gap, and states the two behaviours (real stop when someone is present, in every mode; `bot:blocked` with the question posted when `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1`), the exit state (claim released, worktree and draft PR left in place, `BLOCKED` reported to the caller) and the resume path. `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` and every other file the repo-wide grep finds cite the new gate, pinned by a conformance assertion.
6. `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` gains one Skips-table row for this step with a new tag, and `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` passes with the tag present in the citing skill text.
7. The step does not run in design mode and is skipped, with a `SKIP` decision-log entry, for a `fast-lane` run and for a plan under the documented triviality threshold.
8. `docs/skill-graph.md` states each new edge once, and no `SKILL.md` restates an edge.
9. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Added a top-tier plan review before the first build task that catches spec gaps and undecided behaviour early, and stops the build for a human decision when the spec cannot answer.

## Technical Approach

The reviewer reads two files and returns a findings table in Template A shape with an added `Class` column (spec gap / undecided behaviour / cross-task contract) so the controller routes mechanically rather than paraphrasing. The controller (the `/build` session) applies the per-class handling; the reviewer is read-only. Placement relative to Common Step 1.7 (Design Pre-Build) is the builder's call; running the plan review before 1.7 is recommended because plan amendments should land before design references are pre-loaded for implementers.

### Data / API Surface

- Output template (builder finalizes): `| Severity | Class | Resolution | Path:Line | Finding | Evidence | Suggested resolution |`, "No findings." when clean, at most 7 rows with a "+N more" row, trailing `STATUS: {WORD}` line. `Resolution` is filled only for spec-gap rows and `Evidence` must cite a spec sentence for `intent-resolvable`. Routing keys on Class and Resolution, never on Severity; `low` and `info` findings are logged only and amend nothing.
- Decision-log entries per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`: `AUTO` for an amendment applied, `SKIP` for a skipped step. No `STAGED` entry: nothing is staged.
- Human-needed gate in headless runs: a `gh issue comment` carrying the question, then `bot:blocked` (bootstrapped per `_shared/label-bootstrap.md`) and removal of `auto:*` grants, mirroring `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` Settle steps 5-6 but without the retry-ceiling counter (this gate blocks directly).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-review.md` — new file (name is the builder's call): the full procedure
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — new Common Step pointer between 1.5 and 2 (45,995 bytes now; 51,200 ceiling)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — new HARD-GATE entry for the human-needed spec gap
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` — restates the HARD-GATE families (line 36); add the new gate
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` — new Skips-table row and tag
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — read-only: the contract the dispatch follows
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — read-only: entry schema
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — read-only: the blocked-record transport to reuse
- `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js` — read-only: Capable resolution
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — new edge(s) in the `## build` section
- `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` — roster pin the new row must satisfy
- `tests/build-dispatch-subfile-table-completeness.test.js` — checks `build/` sub-files are listed where required; the new file must satisfy it

## Gotchas

- Steering principle for the whole decomposition: claude-tweaks never files upstream with superpowers and never contradicts SDD's text. This step runs before SDD starts and adds a review SDD does not have; it must not instruct SDD to skip or alter its own pre-flight scan.
- The materialized spec lives in the worktree's copy of `work/{n}-spec.md` in worktree mode, not under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, and reaches the main checkout only on merge (`plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md`). Amend that copy — amending a path under the run directory silently edits nothing the later phases read (`[IL-127]` shadow-copy hazard).
- Anti-goal: a plan review that rules on spec gaps in the SDD ledger only, leaving the spec that `/test`, `/review` and `/wrap-up` judge against unchanged. The amendment must land in the materialized spec.
- Anti-goal: any new mid-flow stop in `auto` mode that is not added to the auto-mode contract's HARD-GATE list deliberately. The human-needed spec gap is that deliberate addition; every other finding class resolves without a stop.
- The Capable reviewer is a dispatch the Subagent Contract governs: `Frontier` is reserved for contract-enumerated singleton slots, so this stays Capable regardless of `profile=frontier`.
- "Someone is present" means `DISPATCH_HEADLESS` is not `1`. `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` (First call section) has the dispatching session add `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1` to the `/claude-tweaks:flow` invocation exactly when the firing came from a scheduled Routine drain with nobody present, and omit it when a human typed the command. Interactive `/flow` in `auto` where the user has since walked away is accepted as "present" (the stop waits for them); that is the stated cost of making this a real stop. ASSUMPTION — verify at build: a human-typed `/dispatch #N` runs the build in a Task subagent that cannot call `AskUserQuestion`, so the stop there must surface as a `BLOCKED` report that the dispatching session (where the human is) relays — via reading `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Settle handling of a `BLOCKED` build call and `_shared/headless-self-report.md`; define that relay in this record rather than leaving a stop nobody can answer.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the retry-ceiling path in Settle is not the right mechanism for this gate (a human-needed spec gap should block on the first occurrence, not after three failed attempts) — via reading `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` steps 5-6 and `_shared/issue-claims.md`'s rule that `bot:blocked` removes all `auto:*` labels.
- The new HARD-GATE row is a contract change under the repo's expand-contract discipline: add the row, update every consumer that enumerates the HARD-GATE list, and never rename an existing gate. Known consumers at record-writing time (2026-10-17): `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` line 208 (the row itself) and `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` line 36 (restates the gate families); grep the repo for "plan-audit hard-fails" and "plan validation" to find any others, including under `plugin/skills/flow/` and `plugin/skills/dispatch/`.
- Amending the spec after the plan was written can trip `build/SKILL.md`'s plan-staleness rule on a resumed build ("has the spec evolved since the plan was written?"). Committing the spec amendment together with the plan amendment, in the same commit, is what keeps the pair consistent; say so in the sub-file.
- Decided (2026-10-17): the live record body is never edited and nothing is staged. The record comment is the durable trace on the issue; the worktree's amended spec reaches `main` only on merge. Do not add a Review Console apply path or a new staged-item kind.
- This record shares `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`, `plan-audit.md`, `plan-authoring-checks.md` and `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js` with #3310 (ready, in progress) — build after it merges and re-read the files. Other ready records touching `build/SKILL.md` (#3118, #3079, #3060, #3004) and `build/dispatch.md` (#3118, #3004, #2869) may land first; expect rebasing, and `docs/skill-graph.md` is shared with #3033.
- Measure byte headroom before adding to `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`: 5,205 bytes remain. The pointer must be a few lines; everything else lives in the new sub-file.
- Trivial-plan threshold: reuse Step 1.5's existing triviality language ("fewer than 3 file references and no `Scope keywords:`") unless the builder can justify a different measure; do not invent a second definition of "trivial" without citing why.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3335, #3212, #3368, #3289

## Current State

#3335 (PR #3369, merged as 77ed997bf) made `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` pass `auto` explicitly on both Task-call `/claude-tweaks:flow` commands, so a project with `auto-mode: default-off` no longer resolves a dispatched, headless call to `interactive`. That guarantee lives only in prose. It holds only if the dispatched agent runs the command text verbatim, and #3212 documents first-call agents that paraphrase or skip parts of `/flow`.

Today `/claude-tweaks:flow` Step 1 (`plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md:117-119`) resolves the mode in this order:

1. An explicit mode keyword.
2. The `auto-mode` policy, where `default-off` gives `interactive`.
3. The intrinsic `auto`.

Step 1 never consults the run's own dispatch binding, even though that binding is already on disk when Step 1 runs. `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` Step 5 runs `hooks.js record-worktree --run <dir> <wt> --dispatch` before call 1 (`dispatch/sibling-session-check.md`). That call stamps a permanent `dispatched: true` into `{run-dir}/run-state.json` and passes the same directory inline as `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`.

Suppose a dispatched agent runs `/flow` but drops the `auto` token. Under `default-off`, the call resolves to `interactive`. `flow/manifesto.md:17` says interactive mode writes no `config.yml`. `checkDispatchConfigGate` (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`) then denies every git write in the bound worktree, and its remedy tells the agent to run Step 3, which an `interactive` run never does.

The decision on the open question was made on 2026-10-17: yes. A dispatch-bound run resolves to `auto` regardless of the `auto-mode` policy, as a mechanical backstop beside the explicit token.

## Deliverables

1. In `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md` Step 1's mode-resolution list, add a new rung between "Explicit mode keyword" and "`auto-mode` policy". When `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is set, resolves under `$RUN_ROOT` (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`'s anchoring check), and its `run-state.json` parses with `dispatched: true`, the mode is `auto`. Any other outcome falls through to the `auto-mode` policy rung unchanged. That covers an unset variable, a directory outside `$RUN_ROOT`, a missing or unparseable `run-state.json`, and `dispatched` absent or not `true`.
2. Record the resolved mode's source so the run shows why it is `auto`. The Manifesto's Mode row (`flow/manifesto.md`, row 1) and its log line name the source as the dispatch binding, for example `auto (dispatched run)`. Do not write a `decisions.md` line at Step 1, for the reason given in Gotchas.
3. Update `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`:
   - The mode table's `interactive` row and the **Default note** must state that `auto-mode: default-off` does not lower a `/flow` run whose run dir is bound `dispatched: true`.
   - An explicit mode keyword still outranks that binding.
4. Update every other restatement of "`default-off` → `interactive`" that claims to describe `/flow` so it carries the dispatched-run exception. At minimum that includes `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema.md`'s `auto-mode` row. Grep the repo for further restatements, including in docs and journeys.
5. Add a new `node --test` prose-conformance pin. It must assert three things against the live `flow/SKILL.md`: the rung exists, it sits after the explicit-keyword rung, and it sits before the `auto-mode` policy rung. It must also assert the contract's dispatched-run sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `flow/SKILL.md` Step 1 lists four mode-resolution rungs in this order: explicit keyword, then the dispatch binding (`run-state.json` `dispatched: true` → `auto`), then the `auto-mode` policy, then intrinsic `auto`.
- The dispatch-binding rung names its fall-through cases explicitly: unset `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, a run dir that fails the `$RUN_ROOT` anchoring check, a missing or unparseable `run-state.json`, and `dispatched` not `true`. Each falls through to the `auto-mode` policy rung, and none of them stops the run.
- An explicit `interactive`, `hybrid`, or `confirm` keyword on a dispatch-bound run still wins. The new rung sits below rung 1, never above it.
- On a dispatch-bound run that resolved through the new rung, the Manifesto's Mode row names the dispatch binding as the mode's source.
- `_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s `interactive` row and Default note both state the dispatched-run exception. `_shared/policy-schema.md`'s `auto-mode` row does too.
- The new test fails when the rung is removed from `flow/SKILL.md`, which can be shown by reverting the rung. It also fails when the rung is moved above the explicit-keyword rung.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Dispatched pipeline runs stay hands-off even if the dispatched agent paraphrases its command line.

## Technical Approach

Step 1 reads `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR/run-state.json` directly and does not route through `resolve-policy.js`. The dispatch binding is run state, not policy, and `resolve-policy.js` walks only `config.yml` → `policy.yml` → the schema default. That walk cannot be the source here, because `config.yml` is exactly what the Manifesto has not written yet.

Use one plain `node -e` read that prints `dispatched` or nothing. It must be fail-open: any exception prints nothing, so the rung falls through. Anchor the path check with the same rule Step 3's adoption already applies (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`), so a worktree-trapped `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is never trusted `[IL-127]`.

The test follows `tests/dispatch-flow-explicit-auto-mode.test.js`'s pattern: live-prose slicing of the `### Step 1: Validate Input` section, with an ordering assertion on the numbered rung list.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md` — Step 1 mode resolution gains the dispatch-binding rung
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — Mode row (row 1) and its log line name the dispatch binding as source
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — `interactive` row and Default note state the dispatched-run exception
- `plugin/skills/_shared/policy-schema.md` — `auto-mode` row carries the dispatched-run exception
- `tests/flow-dispatched-run-auto-mode.test.js` — new prose pin for the rung's presence, its order, and the contract sentence

## Gotchas

- This record is blocked by #3368, which is in flight in PR #3383. That record rewrites the same `policy-schema.md` `auto-mode` row's default and meaning columns, and pins them in `tests/auto-mode-scope-conformance.test.js`. Build this record on top of that merge. Add the dispatched-run exception to #3368's corrected wording, and keep #3368's pin green. Do not edit the row against the pre-#3368 text.
- Do not log at Step 1 into `decisions.md`. Step 3's adoption check (`flow/steps-and-gates.md` case 2) treats a minted run dir as adoptable only while its `decisions.md` holds nothing beyond Step 2.8's claim-log lines. The `dispatched: true` marker pattern added in #3242 also admits it, but adding a Step 1 line widens what that check must tolerate. Surface the source through the Manifesto instead.
- This backstop covers only an agent that runs `/flow` with `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` and drops the `auto` token. It does nothing for #3212's bypass class, where the agent never invokes `/flow` at all or skips its steps. `checkDispatchConfigGate` and the two-call gate's post-hoc artifact check remain the guards there.
- `checkDispatchConfigGate`'s remedy text still says "run its Step 3". With this rung in place, an `interactive` dispatched run can arise only from an explicit `interactive` keyword. The remedy text is out of scope here, because the decision covered the backstop only.
- Grep the repo-wide restatements of the `default-off` rule before writing the pin. A pin limited to `flow/SKILL.md` misses copies elsewhere, which is the anti-pattern recorded in `.claude/skills/skill-prose-conformance-tests/SKILL.md` after #3335.

## Original request

/flow: treat a dispatch-bound run as auto regardless of auto-mode policy (backstop for #3335)

Origin: reflect light from #3335

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

#3335 made `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` pass `auto` explicitly on both Task-call `/claude-tweaks:flow` commands, so a project with `auto-mode: default-off` no longer resolves a dispatched (headless) call to `interactive`. The guarantee is prose-only: it holds only if the dispatched agent runs the command text verbatim. #3212 documents first-call agents that bypass or paraphrase `/flow`. Such an agent can drop the `auto` token. Under `default-off` the call then resolves to `interactive`, skips Step 3, and `checkDispatchConfigGate` denies every commit with a remedy (run Step 3) that `interactive` mode never performs.

## Deliverables

Decide whether `/claude-tweaks:flow` Step 1 mode resolution should treat a run bound `dispatched: true` (`hooks.js record-worktree --dispatch`) as `auto` regardless of the `auto-mode` policy, as a mechanical backstop beside the explicit token.

If yes: add the rule to Step 1, which runs before Step 3 adopts the dispatch-minted run directory, and pin it with a test.

## Open Question

Should a dispatched run's `dispatched: true` binding outrank the project `auto-mode` policy inside `/flow` itself, so that `auto` no longer relies on prose alone? Or is the explicit token plus `checkDispatchConfigGate`'s deny enough? The cost of the change is a new precedence input in `_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s chain.

## Release Note

Dispatched pipeline runs stay hands-off even if the dispatched agent paraphrases its command line.

**Related:** #3335 #1944

Origin: /claude-tweaks:specify shaping of #3335

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/issues/near-duplicate.js`'s body-anchor signal (`extractCurrentStateAnchors`) collects every backtick span in `## Current State` except those `isGenericAnchor` rejects. Skill-name spans such as `/flow` and `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` pass that filter, so any two records that mention the same skill score a `body-anchor-overlap` hit. `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md`'s Near-duplicate candidate check then refuses to shape a record when any candidate, even a score-1 match on this signal alone, is `ready` with an open linked PR or `bot:in-progress`.

Observed shaping #3335 (2026-10-17): 29 candidates out of 151 open records, 27 of them score-1 `body-anchor-overlap` only. #3002 (`verify.js` stamp chunking) and #3048 (QA story selection) matched only on `/flow` and `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`. Both are `ready` with open PR #3332, so the procedure would have refused #3335 and posted an "Absorb into #3002" decision. The refusal was overridden by hand. The procedure also contradicts itself: "the finder never blocks shaping on its own signal alone" versus "the one automatic refusal the finder's signal authorizes on its own".

## Deliverables

1. `isGenericAnchor` rejects skill-name anchors: a span matching `^/[a-z0-9:-]+$` (a slash command such as `/flow` or `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`).
2. `shaping-mode.md`'s automatic absorb refusal requires a candidate scoring at least 2 signals; a score-1 candidate is surfaced in the table and the `**Related:**` line only. The "never blocks shaping on its own signal alone" sentence is reconciled with the refusal rule.
3. Regression tests in the near-duplicate suite: two records sharing only `/flow` and `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` anchors produce no `body-anchor-overlap` signal, and a real file-path anchor still does.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `findNearDuplicates` returns no `body-anchor-overlap` signal for a pair whose only shared Current State anchors are slash-command names.
2. A pair sharing a repo file-path anchor (for example `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md`) still yields `body-anchor-overlap`.
3. `shaping-mode.md`'s refusal paragraph names the minimum score of 2, and a prose-conformance assertion pins it.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Shaping a record no longer proposes absorbing it into an unrelated record that merely mentions the same skill.

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential
Origin: reflect light from #3337

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow` Step 2.8 mints the run directory (`resolve-run-dir --create`) and then immediately writes the claim-log line into its `decisions.md` (`flow/claim-targets.md`, #2492), before Step 3 writes `config.yml` or any `run-state.json` exists.

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` `isUnadoptedMint` (line 54) excludes a mint from fallback event attribution only while it carries neither `run-state.json` nor `decisions.md`. Once the claim line lands, the mint is an unowned, newest, non-terminal run, so `post-tool-use.js`'s fallback attribution (`attribution: 'fallback'`) routes sibling sessions' events into its `events.jsonl`.

`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js:145` then computes `hasOtherContent = decisionsHasContent || nonEmpty(events.jsonl) || specMaterialized`, so a fresh mint with only foreign fallback events adopts as **case 3** (repair: backfill worktree, PR, materialize) instead of **case 2** (fresh). #3242 fixed the same misclassification for Step 1.5/1.8 `decisions.md` content; the `events.jsonl` arm is untouched.

Observed in run `2026-10-17T075913-spec-3337` (#3337): within 30 seconds of the claim, `events.jsonl` held three foreign lines — a `claude-tweaks:dispatch` `skill_invoked` and two `session-end` events from sessions `2a784df0…` and `57ef0028…`, all `"attribution":"fallback"` — and `flow-preflight.js` reported `case: 3` with backfills `worktree registration, PR-early lifecycle, materialize commit`. The orchestrator had to override the case by hand.

## Deliverables

- `isUnadoptedMint` treats a directory whose `decisions.md` classifies as `claim-log-only` (`bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js` `classifyDecisions`) and that has no `run-state.json` as still unadopted, so fallback attribution never targets it.
- `computeAdoption` ignores `events.jsonl` lines carrying `"attribution":"fallback"` when deciding `hasOtherContent` (only `env`/`session`-attributed events are evidence this run did anything).
- A regression test for each: a claim-log-only mint is skipped by the fallback resolver; a mint whose `events.jsonl` holds only fallback-attributed lines adopts as case 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a minted run dir holding only a Step 2.8 claim line, a hook event from a different session with no `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is not appended to that dir's `events.jsonl`.
2. `flow-preflight.js --run <dir>` on a dir with a claim-log-only `decisions.md` and an `events.jsonl` holding only `"attribution":"fallback"` lines reports `adoption.value.case === 2`.
3. A dir whose `events.jsonl` holds an `env`- or `session`-attributed line still reports `hasOtherContent: true`.

## Release Note

A freshly claimed `/flow` run no longer picks up other sessions' hook events, and no longer misreads them as an interrupted earlier run.

# Reflect — staged finding 4

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #2927

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` reads open-items ledger rows with `row.split('|')` (line 339), then takes `cells[3]` as the Status. GFM tables escape a literal pipe inside a cell as `\|`, but the split does not honor the escape. An escaped pipe in the Item cell shifts every later cell, so the Status the pack reads is a fragment of the Item text.

Observed on #2927's wrap-up, 2026-10-17: ledger row 12's Item quoted `Surface: web\|mobile\|desktop`. `wrap-up-pack.js` reported `unrecognized: 1` with value `mobile\`. The row's real status was `open`.

The dangerous case is an **open** row with an escaped pipe. It counts as `unrecognized`, not `open`, so `pack.ledger.open` under-counts. The nothing-left-behind gate's open-item enforcement then misses it, and only #2080's non-blocking warning line shows anything is wrong.

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow` (line 106) splits the same way. It refuses a row whose cell count is not 7, so it fails loudly: an escaped-pipe row cannot be resolved through it.

## Deliverables

1. One shared ledger-row cell splitter that treats `\|` as a literal pipe inside a cell. It splits only on unescaped `|` and keeps the escape intact when serializing back.
2. Use it in `pack.js`'s ledger count and in `ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow`. Check the repo's other ledger-table readers and point any that split rows the same way at it too.
3. Tests: a row whose Item cell holds `a\|b` counts under its real status in the pack, and `flipLedgerRow` resolves it without the shape refusal. The serialized row must keep the `\|`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An open ledger row whose Item contains `\|` is counted as `open` by `wrap-up-pack.js`, not `unrecognized`.
- `flipLedgerRow` resolves such a row, and the written row is byte-identical apart from the Status and Resolution cells.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Wrap-up no longer miscounts an open ledger item whose text contains an escaped pipe, so it can't slip past the nothing-left-behind check.

# Reflect — staged finding 2

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #2927

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js`'s `renderGit` (line 204) runs `execSync('git status --porcelain -b', { cwd })` on every statusline render. It passes no `--no-optional-locks` flag and no `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. A plain `git status` takes the index lock opportunistically to refresh its stat cache.

The statusline re-renders around every tool call. In a worktree-isolated session, the session's own index-writing git commands race that render and fail with `fatal: Unable to create '.../.git/worktrees/{name}/index.lock': File exists`. The colliding commands are the Bash tool's plain `git merge`, `git add` and `git commit`. The lock is gone a moment later, so the failure looks stale. That misleads an agent into deleting the lock, or into blaming `npm test`, the cause the existing guidance names.

Observed on #2927's run, 2026-10-17:
- `git merge origin/main` (the post-creation catch-up) failed 4 times in a row.
- `git commit` and several `git add` calls failed, and passed only on retry.
- The same commands run from a node `execFileSync` wrapper succeeded on the first attempt.
- `ps` showed a `git status --porcelain -b` process during the failures.

## Deliverables

1. Make `renderGit`'s status call lock-free: `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain -b`, or `env: { ...process.env, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: '0' }`. Keep the existing branch/dirty parsing unchanged.
2. Add a test that pins the lock-free form, for example by asserting that the exec runner receives the flag or env. Follow the existing statusline test's injectable-runner seam if there is one; otherwise add the minimal seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The statusline's git status call never takes `.git/index.lock`: the command carries `--no-optional-locks`, or the spawn env sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
- The branch and dirty-dot rendering is unchanged for clean, dirty, detached and no-commits repos.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

The statusline no longer makes your own git commands fail with an index.lock error while it refreshes.

_Filed by `reflect`. Close to resolve; label `wontfix` to suppress future reports of this finding._

Origin: dispatch session 2026-10-16/17 (PR #3325 merge, close-out of #3240/#3292)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

A dispatched second-call agent (pr-first, fast-lane bundle #2908/#2918/#2934, PR #3325) composed its `gh pr merge -t/-b` arguments by `eval`-ing `compose-subject.js --shell` output, as `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 3 prescribes. A shell-variable bug leaked literal debug text (`SUBJECT_BODY=...`) and a duplicated body into the squash commit `770e574ea`. The agent then rewrote `main` with `git commit-tree` + `git push --force-with-lease` (new tip `9c9f5e722`).

Tree and parent were identical and no other PR merged in between, so no content was lost. But PR #3325's recorded `mergeCommit` now points off-`main` (any merged-PR landed-proof keyed on it now answers wrong) and the rewritten commit carries a different author email.

Gaps:
1. Nothing in `_shared/pr-first-merge.md`, `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md`, or `dispatch/task-prompt.md` forbids force-pushing or otherwise rewriting the integration branch. The only correct response to a botched merge message is to leave it and report it.
2. Step 3's `eval "$SUBJECT_EXPORTS"` then `-t "$SUBJECT_TITLE" -b "$SUBJECT_BODY"` composition is fragile. Writing the CLI's JSON form to files and passing `--body-file` (used cleanly for the #3240 and #3292 close-out merges) avoids shell interpretation of the body entirely.
3. `gh pr merge --auto` on this repo also failed with `Protected branch rules not configured for this branch (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)`. Step 3 branch 1's auto-merge-not-enabled signature (`Auto merge is not allowed` / `auto-merge` + `not allowed|not enabled`) does not match that wording, so it falls to branch 5 (ready+comment) instead of the `merge-when-green` wait row.

## Deliverables

- An explicit prohibition, stated once in `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` and cited (not restated) from the dispatch Task templates: never force-push, reset, or rewrite the integration branch; on a malformed merge message, log it and report `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`.
- Step 3's merge invocation composes title/body from `compose-subject.js`'s JSON output via files (`-t` from a file read, body via `--body-file`), never `eval` of `--shell` output — every merge fence that cites Step 3 migrated.
- Step 3 branch 1's signature also matches the `Protected branch rules not configured` wording.
- Tests pinning all three.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` contains a rule forbidding force-push/rewrite of the integration branch, and `dispatch/task-prompt.md`'s second-call template cites it; a conformance test asserts both.
- [ ] No merge fence in `plugin/skills/**` uses `eval` of `compose-subject.js --shell` output to build `gh pr merge` arguments; a sweep test asserts it.
- [ ] Step 3 branch 1's signature classifier routes `GraphQL: Pull request Protected branch rules not configured for this branch (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)` to the auto-merge-not-enabled branch; a test with that literal stderr asserts the routing.

## Release Note

Pipeline merges can no longer rewrite the main branch, and a merge commit message can no longer be garbled by shell quoting.

Origin: reflect full mode from #3249 (Surprises + Near-misses lenses)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #3326

## Current State

During #3249's review (14 lens agents, 7 reproduction pairs at `review-effort: high`), lens 3a's (Convention) reproduction pair disagreed: one agent (3a-A) returned no findings; the other (3a-B) returned `STATUS: BLOCKED`, citing several specific functions, exports, and parameters as "completely missing from the codebase" — with exact line-number citations drawn from the record's own materialized plan file (which shows the code to add). Every one of those claims was false: direct `grep` against the live worktree confirmed every named item already existed exactly as claimed-missing (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js:242,326`; `release-merged.js:16,360,365,385`; `archive-merged.js:320`). The agent appears to have conflated the plan document's own illustrative "add this code" listing with the code's current applied state.

The reproduction-pair mechanism (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`) correctly flagged this as a disagreement, but its own handling treats *any* disagreement as `unconfirmed`/low-confidence, which is the right default for a genuine judgment call but is not the cheapest-available resolution for this specific claim shape: "a named function/export/parameter does not exist" is mechanically, cheaply verifiable (one `grep`/`Read`) before ever reaching a human at the Review Console. Without an explicit instruction to do that check, a differently-briefed session could plausibly have accepted the disagreement as "needs a human to judge" and left a factually-false BLOCKED claim staged as merely low-confidence, sending a human to investigate a non-existent gap.

## Deliverables

- Add one sentence to `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s dispatch prompt template (or the CALIBRATION block) instructing lens agents not to infer code absence from a plan/spec document's own illustrative code listings — verify a "missing code" claim by reading the actual target file directly.
- Add a narrow, mechanical escape hatch to the reproduction-pair disagreement-handling procedure: when one side of a disagreement asserts code/export/parameter *absence* at a named `path:line`/symbol, the dispatching session runs one `grep`/`Read` check against the live target file before staging the finding as `unconfirmed` — a contradicted "missing" claim resolves straight to "refuted, not staged" rather than "low-confidence, staged."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reproduction-pair disagreement where one side asserts code/export/parameter absence that a one-command `grep`/`Read` check can mechanically refute no longer reaches the Wrap-Up Review Console as a merely low-confidence item — it resolves to refuted before routing.
- [ ] The dispatch prompt template explicitly warns against inferring code state from a plan/spec document's own code listings.

## Release Note

Review's reproduction-pair handling gains a cheap ground-truth check for mechanically-falsifiable "code is missing" disagreements, reducing false BLOCKED verdicts reaching the Review Console.

## Current State

`bin/lib/coordination.js` `categoriseReproduction` pairs a same-location candidate (path exact, line ±2) only when `sameSubstance` is not `false`. For two independently worded reports of the same issue, the substance score falls below the threshold, so a genuinely reproduced finding comes out as two `nearLocation` unconfirmed entries.

Observed three times: #3023 (lens 3b, `release.js` `merge-base --is-ancestor` missing `--end-of-options`), #3028 (lens 3f, `tests/bin-lib/compose-subject.test.js:454`, rows copied verbatim), and #3003 (lens 3c, `plugin/bin/qa-stamp.js:121` and `:132`, rows copied verbatim, both pairs split). Each time the controller fell back to the direct-verification override. Re-checked after #2955 widened the location band to ±5: the merged categoriser still returns all four #3003 entries unconfirmed, so the gap is the same-line substance test, not the band. In an unattended run where no source read happens, a reproduced medium finding routes to the Review Console's low-confidence section instead of being auto-applied under the ceiling.

## Deliverables

Make the same-substance decision robust to independent wording for same-file, same-line (±2) pairs. Options: weight shared code identifiers and backticked tokens, or treat an exact-line match plus a shared identifier as same substance.

Keep #1980's guard: two different issues at the same location must still stay split.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fixture test built from the three observed pairs (each agent's Finding text verbatim) categorises every pair as `confirmed`.

#1980's existing near-location, different-substance fixtures still come out `unconfirmed`.

## Release Note

Review reproduction pairs that report the same issue in different words are now recognized as reproduced.

both this run's discarded `RECOMMEND_MERGE` verdict and the live grant that won the race, instead

reverify currently drops the flag-back write with the same generic skip line — it does not
distinguish "a concurrent actor disagreed with this run's own recommendation" from any other

as a related but larger class of disagreement than that record's grant-row-only Technical
Approach covered.

- Extend `refine-mode.md` Step 5's flag-back reverify branch to compare the flag-back row's own
  `RECOMMEND_BUILD` verdict (and rationale) against the live grant state, the same way the grant
  row's comparison (#2719) already does for `RECOMMEND_MERGE`.
- Add the distinguishable skip-line template(s) to `refine-closing-summary.md`'s template list,
  mirroring the grant-row "agreed"/"DIVERGED" shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A flag-back row dropped by the pre-write reverify because a concurrent write granted the
  record logs whether that concurrent grant agreed with or diverged from this run's own

Flag-back rows now log the same concurrent-grant-divergence detail grant rows do when a concurrent actor's decision disagrees with this run's own recommendation.

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/git-command.js`'s `skipGlobalFlags` resolves a `-C` value with `path.resolve(effCwd, value)` (~:297), so `git -C '' commit` targets `path.resolve(cwd)`. With no `-C` at all, `forEachCommandSegment` passes `effCwd = cwd` through verbatim (~:239).

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-agent-trust-scope.md`'s "What NOT to flag" section has no exception for a dimension the project has formally accepted in an ADR, and `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-agent-trust-scope.js` cannot see one.

This repo accepts `network-egress` under `docs/decisions/0022-unattended-runs-keep-network-egress.md` (#2876): `/claude-tweaks:research` needs `WebFetch`, and a narrow deny rule would only silence the finding. So every `/claude-tweaks:code-health focus=agent-trust-scope` sweep, and every `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6.65 pass on a diff touching `.claude/settings.json`, re-reports `network-egress` at medium severity. A judge then re-derives "accepted risk" by hand each time, or a sweep files a duplicate issue for a decided question. Observed on #2876's own review: Step 6.65 returned `["network-egress"]`, and the judge had to cite ADR 0022 manually.

## Deliverables

- Add a "What NOT to flag" bullet to `plugin/skills/_shared/criteria-agent-trust-scope.md` covering a dimension that a committed `docs/decisions/*.md` ADR with `**Status:** accepted` names by the generator's exact kind literal (`registry-access` / `network-egress` / `credential-scope`) as an accepted risk. The judge reports it as an informational "accepted risk — ADR NNNN" line, never as a finding and never as a filed issue.
- Update `plugin/skills/review/focus-criterion-passes.md` Step 6.65's result-handling table with the matching row: an accepted-risk candidate renders as a footer note naming the ADR, not as an Agent Trust Scope finding.
- Keep the guard tight. A dimension that is only mentioned in an ADR, or an ADR whose status is not `accepted` (superseded, proposed), still reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With ADR 0022 accepted, a `/claude-tweaks:code-health focus=agent-trust-scope` sweep of this repo files no `network-egress` issue, and its output names ADR 0022 as the reason.
- With ADR 0022's status changed to anything other than `accepted` (fixture or temp copy), the same sweep reports `network-egress` again.
- An ADR that mentions `network-egress` without accepting it does not suppress the finding.

## Release Note

Agent-trust-scope sweeps and reviews stop re-reporting a dimension your project has formally accepted in an ADR, and show it as an accepted risk instead.

## Current State

`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s "Pre-dispatch listing (scratch-sweep baseline)" step tells the reviewer to run `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all > {ctx-dir}/pre-dispatch-status.txt` immediately after `build-review-context.js build` mints `{ctx-dir}`. The post-fan-out untracked-file sweep then diffs against that file.

Under `worktree-always`, `{ctx-dir}` is `{run}/review-ctx` in the main checkout, outside the reviewing session's worktree. In a worktree-isolated session, neither available path for that write works: the shell redirect into a shared-checkout path is a compound command the harness guard refuses, and the Write tool refuses with "Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path". Observed in #2783's review (2026-10-16): the reviewer had to keep the baseline in its own scratchpad, so the sweep's documented input file never existed.

`plugin/bin/build-review-context.js` already writes into `{ctx-dir}` (it creates `context.md` there), but it never captures this baseline itself.

## Deliverables

1. Make `build-review-context.js build` write `{ctx-dir}/pre-dispatch-status.txt` itself, using `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` run with the cwd set to the branch's worktree. Report its path in the printed JSON line (e.g. a `baselinePath` field).

2. Update `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s Pre-dispatch listing paragraph and its Post-fan-out sweep paragraph to read the CLI-written file, and drop the hand-run redirect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `node plugin/bin/build-review-context.js build --base <ref> --branch HEAD --run <run-dir>`, `<run-dir>/review-ctx/pre-dispatch-status.txt` exists and matches `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` at that moment.

- `step3-lens-dispatch.md` no longer tells the reviewer to write any file under `{ctx-dir}` by hand.

- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Review's untracked-file sweep now works in worktree-isolated sessions: its baseline is captured automatically.

groups.body:
Origin: reflect hindsight from #2783

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

#2783 added `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/post-tool-use-failure.js`, registered in `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` with matcher `Bash` only. It records Claude Code's worktree-isolation refusal of a **Bash** command as a `wd-guard-refusal` event (`HARNESS_ISOLATION_REFUSAL_RE` = "This session is isolated in the worktree … Refusing to run it").

The same harness guard also refuses **Write/Edit** calls aimed at a shared-checkout path, with different wording: "This session is isolated in the worktree <path>. Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path." That refusal fired during #2783's own review (a Write to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/<run>/review-ctx/pre-dispatch-status.txt`). Neither the Bash matcher nor the regex captures it, so `/claude-tweaks:reflect`'s Friction Lens never sees this class of isolation friction.

Not yet measured: whether a Write/Edit isolation refusal fires `PostToolUseFailure` at all, and if it does, what the payload's `error` field holds. #2783's probe measured the Bash refusal only.

## Deliverables

1. Probe empirically (headless `claude -p`, as #2783 did for Bash) whether the harness fires `PostToolUseFailure` for a Write/Edit isolation refusal, and record the payload shape (`tool_name`, `error`).

2. If it fires, widen the `hooks.json` matcher to Write|Edit and teach `post-tool-use-failure.js` the Write/Edit refusal wording. Log `wd-guard-refusal` with `tool: <Write|Edit>`, `reason: harness-worktree-isolation` and the target `file_path` (not file content), via the same `resolveDenialRunDir`. `bash-prefilter.js` needs no change: it already passes every non-Bash payload through (its `tool_name !== 'Bash'` early return).

3. If it does not fire, document that limit in `plugin/skills/reflect/full-mode.md`'s Friction Lens section, beside the existing ad-hoc-session Known-limitation clause.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Write or Edit refused by the worktree-isolation guard appears in `node plugin/bin/friction-events.js --run <dir>` output as a `wd-guard-refusal` event naming the tool, OR `reflect/full-mode.md` states explicitly that this refusal class is not observable.

- An ordinary Write/Edit failure (e.g. a stale-read rejection) is not logged as a guard refusal.

- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Friction logging now also covers worktree-isolation refusals of file edits, not just shell commands.

**Related:** #3249 #3290 #3327

Origin: whole-branch review of #3249 (Finding 3)

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#3249 (branch `worktree-dispatch-record-3249`) makes `archive-merged.js` archive a MERGED run with no `console.json` when its `staged/` holds nothing pending (`decideArchiveCore`'s `hasStagedPending` exception, reached from both `archiveMergedRun` and the by-number fallback). A run whose `staged/` holds real pending items still skips `console-never-rendered` by design — the #657/#1130 protection.

That remaining sub-case can never converge automatically: the fast-lane auto-merge short-circuit (`plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md`) surfaces its console content only as a non-blocking PushNotification FYI and never writes `console.json`, so nothing later resolves the staged items. The #3130 incident run (`.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/2026-10-16T155630-record-3130/`) has exactly this shape: no `console.json`, `staged/reflect-1.md` and `staged/wrap-up-skill-1.md` pending.

`plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md` Step 4.2 says a reconcile failure "is logged and left for the next trigger point". #3249 amended that paragraph to name the exception, but the logged/reported skip itself still does not distinguish a transient gh/network failure (converges later) from a structural `console-never-rendered` with pending staged items (needs a human first). Plain `console-never-rendered` is also deliberately excluded from `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS`, so it never escalates.

## Deliverables

1. Make the post-merge reconcile report distinguish "transient failure, will converge at the next trigger point" from "staged/ holds pending items, needs human action before this run can converge" — in Step 4.2's logged line and in whatever the reconcile result exposes to it (e.g. a distinct skip reason for a MERGED, console-never-rendered run with pending staged items).

2. Evaluate, and record the decision on, having the fast-lane auto-merge short-circuit write a minimal `console.json` recording that its staged items were surfaced via the PushNotification — which would let #3249's archive exception apply even when `staged/` is non-empty. If adopted, implement it with a test; if rejected, record why in the short-circuit file.

3. Decide whether that structurally-stuck sub-case should escalate via `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` / `trackStuckSkip` like `console-never-rendered-pr-closed` does, so it surfaces somewhere a human looks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Step 4.2's log/report line never claims convergence is coming for a run that structurally cannot converge without human action; a test pins the distinct reason or wording.

- A transient gh/network failure is still reported as "left for the next trigger point", unchanged.

- The #657/#1130 protection holds: a run with genuinely pending staged items is never archived out of sight without either a resolved console or an explicit recorded surfacing.

## Release Note

After a fast-lane pr-first merge, a run left with unresolved staged items is reported as needing your attention instead of as cleanup that will finish on its own.

## Current State

`plugin/skills/tidy/scan-procedures.md` collects every `kind: release` residue finding as `[git] {subject} — {evidence} — Backfill`. Since #2882 there are two flavors: `remedy: auto` (a `v*` tag with no CHANGELOG heading) and `remedy: record` (a CHANGELOG heading with no local or remote tag, where tagging released history is a human call).

`plugin/skills/tidy/step-6-auto.md`'s routing table, which gives every recommendation an auto-apply tier per aggressiveness level (`conservative` / `moderate` / `aggressive`), has no **Backfill** row. Neither release flavor has a stated tier, so the step's own rule applies: "a finding class that keeps staging needs a routing row". Found by the journeys curation judge in the #2882 wrap-up and confirmed by grep: the only `Backfill` occurrence in `plugin/skills/tidy/` is the scan-procedures line.

## Deliverables

- A **Backfill** row (or two, one per remedy) in `step-6-auto.md`'s routing table. The `remedy: record` flavor never auto-applies at any tier, because creating or pushing a tag is an outward-facing write. The `remedy: auto` flavor gets an explicit tier for adding the missing CHANGELOG heading.
- `scan-procedures.md`'s release paragraph points at that row instead of carrying the disposition inline, keeping the file within its `tests/release-lifecycle-byte-budget.test.js` bound.
- A conformance test pins that every `— {Action}` verb `scan-procedures.md` emits has a matching routing row in `step-6-auto.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `step-6-auto.md` states a tier for both release-finding flavors at all three aggressiveness levels.
- [ ] The heading-with-no-tag flavor is never Auto-apply at any tier.
- [ ] The new conformance test fails when a scan action verb has no routing row (checked by temporarily deleting the Backfill row).

## Release Note

`/claude-tweaks:tidy` now states how it routes release tag/CHANGELOG mismatches at each aggressiveness level, and never auto-tags released history.

Origin: reflect light from #2882

Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #3297

## Current State

`plugin/skills/_shared/staged-patch.md` requires every staging site to validate its patch with `git apply --check` against the worktree as it stands. Its Console apply section then applies a run's patches one after another, "against the cumulative pipeline state". Nothing checks a patch against the state left by the patches staged before it in the same run.

Observed in run 2026-10-16T181217-spec-2882 (#2882 review): `staged/review-1.patch` and `staged/review-2.patch` both inserted a new test directly above the same anchor line in `tests/bin-lib/residue/probes-observed.test.js`. Each passed `--check` on its own. With review-1 applied, review-2 failed: `error: patch failed: tests/bin-lib/residue/probes-observed.test.js:214`. Only an extra stacking check, run by hand outside the contract, caught this. Without it, the console would have taken the description-only fallback for a patch that was valid when staged.

## Deliverables

- `staged-patch.md`'s staging gate also checks each new patch stacked on the run's already-staged `.patch` files, in console order: apply the earlier ones to a scratch copy (or a temporary index via `git apply --cached` against a throwaway `GIT_INDEX_FILE`), then `--check` the new one.
- When the stacked check fails but the solo check passes, the staging site re-derives the diff against the stacked state, or re-anchors the hunk, before writing the artifact. If neither works, it logs the conflict in the STAGED line.
- A test pins that two patches with the same insertion anchor are caught at staging time, not at the console.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Staging a second patch whose hunk context is invalidated by an earlier patch from the same run is reported at staging time, naming both patch paths.
- [ ] Patches that stack cleanly stage exactly as they do today, with no extra log noise.
- [ ] The Console apply section's cumulative-order wording and the staging gate describe the same order.

## Release Note

Staged code-fix proposals are now checked against each other at staging time, so a later patch no longer silently falls back to the description path at the Review Console.

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #2999,#3000
Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #3245 #3335 #3336

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow/SKILL.md`'s Step 3 ("Pipeline Config Manifesto") states it runs in every mode
except `interactive`, writing `config.yml` and initializing `decisions.md`'s config snapshot
header before Step 4 begins — and Step 1.8 states the open-items ledger is created unconditionally
before Step 2's pre-flight checks. On this run (dispatch bundle `2026-10-16T180901-record-2999`,
covering #2999 and #3000), a first `/flow "#2999,#3000" build,test` call completed build and test
successfully (two real commits, a draft PR opened, `TEST_PASSED=true` logged) but left no trace of
either step ever running: no `config.yml` existed anywhere under the run directory or its would-be
`spec-2999/`/`spec-3000/` subdirectories, and no open-items ledger existed at
`docs/plans/*-record-2999*-ledger.md`. `decisions.md`'s `## /flow` section began directly at
"Step 2.8: claimed #2999" with no preceding Manifesto log line. This second call (review, polish,
wrap-up) had to backfill both — writing `config.yml` via `set-config.js`, scaffolding the per-spec
subdirectories per `multispec-config-scaffold.md`, and creating the ledger via `ledger/SKILL.md`'s
Create operation — before continuing, per this call's own explicit instruction not to skip the
Manifesto write.

## Deliverables

- Investigate whether `/flow`'s Step 3 and Step 1.8 have a code path that returns without writing
  `config.yml`/creating the ledger when invoked as the first of a dispatch bundle's two planned
  calls (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up`) — e.g. an early-return before Step 3 on some
  input shape, or a step-list check that (incorrectly) ties the Manifesto/ledger write to the
  presence of `review`/`wrap-up` in the resolved step list.
- Add a `node --test` assertion (or a prose self-check) that a `/flow` run reaching Step 4 for
  ANY step list always has `config.yml` and a ledger file by that point, so a future regression
  here surfaces mechanically instead of being caught by a second call's own defensive instructions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The root cause (or: "no defect found — these two runs are explained by {reason}") is identified
  and written up.
- Either a fix lands, or this record is closed with the explanation if investigation finds the
  gap was something else entirely (e.g. operator/dispatch-prompt behavior rather than `/flow`
  skill-prose/implementation).

## Release Note

N/A (internal tooling correctness).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/SKILL.md` — Step 3, Step 1.8
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md`
- `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md`, `multispec-config-scaffold.md`

## Current State

Under `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s two-call pattern (`/flow {target} build,test` then, in a fresh
Task-tool dispatch, `/flow {target} review,polish,wrap-up` against the same run dir), the first
call's `/test` phase logged its result to `decisions.md` as a plain summary line
(`npm test: full suite green at HEAD {sha}: {n} pass, 0 fail, {m} skipped`) rather than through
`test/verification.md`'s stamped `verify.js` invocation, which writes the runner-level pass stamp
`verify.js --stamp-status` reads. On this run (#3034), the second call's review Step 1.5
(`node bin/verify.js --stamp-status`) found `present: false` at the same HEAD the first call had
already verified, so it had no choice but to re-run the full suite from scratch (~117s) rather
than trusting the first call's already-passing result.

## Deliverables

1. Confirm whether `/claude-tweaks:test`'s own invocation path always writes the stamp, or
   whether some call shape (standalone CLI, a particular dispatch route) can log a pass without
   it, as observed here.
2. If a gap exists, close it so a `/flow {target} build,test` first call's test phase always
   leaves a stamp the second call's review-gate can trust.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh two-call dispatch run (`build,test` then `review,polish,wrap-up` against the same
  `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`) shows `verify.js --stamp-status` returning `verifiedHead: true` at the
  second call's review Step 1.5, with no full-suite re-run.

## Release Note

No user-visible change — internal pipeline-plumbing fix so a dispatched two-call run's second
call trusts the first call's own test pass instead of re-running it.

## Suggested resolution

Audit `/claude-tweaks:test`'s dispatch-context code path (the one `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s first
call invokes) against `test/verification.md`'s stamped-invocation requirement; add the stamp
write there if missing.

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Nothing shipped can put `/claude-tweaks:code-health focus=security-hardening` on a schedule:

- `plugin/skills/routine/fleet.md`'s composition table gives four code-health verticals a scheduled row each: `dead-code`, `test-hygiene`, `abstraction-police` and `experiment-cleanup` (rows 1-4). `security-hardening` has no row.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/routine-template-schema.md` says the `focus` field is unset in every shipped template and is "supplied at fleet-provisioning time". `/claude-tweaks:routine create code-health` takes no focus argument. The fleet is therefore the only shipped way to schedule a focus vertical.
- The daily generalist sweep (fleet row 5, or a standalone `routine create code-health`) never applies this criterion. `plugin/bin/lib/code-health/criteria.js` marks `security-hardening` as "pinned directly by code-health's focus=security-hardening ... never selected via criteriaForArea". The generalist applies `security-logic` and `iac-security` only, one rotated slice per firing.

Today the criterion runs in only two places. `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 6.6 (`plugin/skills/review/focus-criterion-passes.md`) runs it diff-scoped and report-only, and only on reviews of pipeline-built work. Otherwise someone has to run `/claude-tweaks:code-health focus=security-hardening` by hand.

A focus firing that finds nothing costs almost nothing. `plugin/skills/code-health/focus-mode.md` makes a firing with zero candidates a no-op, and dedup against open `by:code-health` issues keeps a repeat firing from filing the same finding twice. The generator (`plugin/bin/lib/code-health/candidates-security-hardening.js`) is shaped for app repos: client and route directory heuristics, AI SDK calls, JWT calls, upload handlers and webhooks. On a repo without those shapes, a daily firing ends at the no-op.

Out of scope here: the other focus verticals without a fleet row (`agent-trust-scope`, `app-store-readiness`, `prelaunch`), any per-commit or diff-scoped firing mode, and any auto-prepared fixes. The #3052 evaluation recommends against the last two.

## Deliverables

1. Add a `security-hardening` row to `fleet.md`'s composition table: Vertical finder bucket, source `skills/code-health/routine-template.yml`, `focus` override `security-hardening`, PREFIXED_NAME `{REPO_SLUG}-code-health-security-hardening`. Give it a daily cron that keeps the stagger rationale true (finders before the 08:00 shaping unit; `0 7 * * *` is a candidate). Update the stagger-rationale paragraph to match.
2. Migrate every literal that hardcodes the vertical-finder row range or the code-health instance count. That covers `fleet.md` ("rows 1-4", "all five code-health instances (rows 1-5)", "Row 5", "rows 6-12", "row 5-12", and the Step 6 and RECONCILE "rows 1-4" mentions) and `routine-template-schema.md`'s `focus` field row ("rows 1-4"). Prefer count-free phrasing (for example "the Vertical finder rows"), in line with fleet.md's own cardinality-drift rule.
3. Update any test or code that pins the fleet composition. Candidates from a grep: `plugin/bin/lib/issues/fleet-counters.js`, `tests/routine-fleet-status-off.test.js`, `tests/routine-pause-resume.test.js`, `tests/routine-webhook-trigger.test.js`, `tests/backlog-refine-headless.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/anti-patterns.test.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fleet.md`'s composition table has a Vertical finder row whose `focus` override is `security-hardening`. Its PREFIXED_NAME is `{REPO_SLUG}-code-health-security-hardening`, and its cron is distinct from every other row's.
- `git grep -n -E "rows 1-4|rows 1-5|rows 6-12|row 5-12|five code-health instances" -- plugin/skills/routine plugin/skills/_shared/routine-template-schema.md` returns nothing.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

`/claude-tweaks:routine fleet on` now also schedules a daily `code-health focus=security-hardening` sweep, so the pre-launch security hardening checks run without a manual invocation.
