groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

Claude Code 2.1.283+ ships a built-in `/prompt-audit` command. It reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, and flags instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules (source in the original request below).

What claude-tweaks already has in this space:

- `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md`) audits `.claude/skills/*.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md` and CLAUDE.md against the codebase, a template, and best practice, one target per firing. It then files `by:harness-health` issues. Its stated scope is the project's own `.claude/` tree (this repo has 17 files under `.claude/skills/`), not the 39 shipped `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` files. Its target discovery reads only `<root>/.claude/skills` (`plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/scope.js:198`).
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is a manual checklist to re-run whenever a new Claude model ships. It covers model-version deltas and a verification/self-check instruction audit against `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md`. That is the "instructions written for older models" concern, done by hand.

So the open question has two parts: what `/prompt-audit` catches that neither harness-health nor the manual model-version checklist catches, and whether it reaches the shipped `plugin/skills/` library at all.

## Deliverables

1. Run `/prompt-audit` once against this repo's CLAUDE.md, `.claude/skills/`, `plugin/skills/`, and `plugin/agents/`, and keep its raw output.
2. A comparison, posted as a comment on this record, that sorts each finding into one of three buckets:
   - already covered by harness-health (name the harness-health check);
   - already covered by the model-version prompting checklist in `docs/skill-authoring.md`;
   - genuinely new.
3. For each genuinely new finding, take exactly one of two routes:
   - a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body, either fixing the flagged instruction or extending harness-health or the checklist to catch that class;
   - a stated reason, in the comment, why it is not worth acting on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/prompt-audit` has been run once over the targets in Deliverable 1. The comment states the Claude Code version used and the target set actually covered.
- Every finding in the run's output appears in the comparison comment under exactly one of the three buckets.
- Every genuinely new finding has either a linked filed backlog record or a stated reason for no action; none is left unrouted.
- The comment states whether `/prompt-audit` reached the `plugin/skills/` library, since harness-health does not.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of Claude Code's `/prompt-audit` against claude-tweaks' own harness-health audit.

## Technical Approach

Run `/prompt-audit` from an interactive session at the repo root. Then work through its findings against two references: harness-health's analysis criteria (`plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`, the shared judge procedure) and the model-version checklist. Fixes to individual skills are not made in this record; they are filed as follow-ups so each lands with its own conformance-test run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — the existing audit whose coverage is compared
- `plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` — harness-health's shared judge procedure
- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — the manual model-version prompting checklist (line 215)
- `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md` — the levers that checklist audits against

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `/prompt-audit` can be run on demand in this environment and accepts the `plugin/` subtree as a target. It is a built-in slash command, so a headless agent may not be able to invoke it the same way. Confirm before relying on an unattended run.
- Fixing a flagged skill instruction here would touch shipped prose that conformance tests pin repo-wide (`tests/` byte-pins skill text). That is why fixes go to follow-up records, each with its own full-suite run.
- harness-health's own scope is `.claude/` by design. A finding that it misses on `plugin/skills/` is a scope question, not automatically a harness-health defect.

## Original request

Run /prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md and skills

Current State:
- Claude Code's /prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, flagging instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules.
- claude-tweaks ships a large skill library that has not been audited against the new Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 models this way.
- claude-tweaks' own harness-health skill does a related but not identical audit.

Deliverables:
- Run /prompt-audit prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own repo.
- Compare its findings against what harness-health already catches; fold in anything harness-health misses.

Acceptance Criteria:
- /prompt-audit run once with findings reviewed.
- Any genuinely new findings (not already covered by harness-health) turned into follow-up fixes or a harness-health improvement.

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog#2-1-283

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3047

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:test`'s pipeline path with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:70`) selects QA stories by `source_files` ∩ `node bin/verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}`. `--changed-files` (`plugin/bin/verify.js:156`, `changedFilesMode`) resolves its base through `resolveBase` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js:54`) with this precedence: `--base` first, then the checkout's own verification-stamp anchor whenever it is usable and not equal to HEAD (`:62-77`), and only then the `--integration-branch` merge-base (`:78-84`).

In a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the stamp. Bookkeeping commits follow (for example `/stories` committing a new story YAML), so by the time `/test` selects stories the stamp anchor is an ancestor of HEAD but not HEAD. The changed-file set is then only the post-stamp bookkeeping, never the build's own source changes. Observed (reporter, plugin 6.136.0): the set was a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in it, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components. The reporter selected stories by hand against `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`.

The stamp anchor is the right base for re-running tests (`affected`, `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table): the stamp records what was already verified. It is the wrong base for QA story selection, because the stamp says nothing about QA. `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md:9` reads the same `--changed-files` set to decide which files the design CLI gate judges, so it has the same blind spot.

## Deliverables

1. Add an opt-in `--ignore-stamp` flag to `verify.js --changed-files` (parsed in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js`, honored by `changedFilesMode`/`resolveBase`). It skips the stamp anchor and resolves the base from `--base` or the `--integration-branch` merge-base, keeping the existing exit-1 and `warning: resolved base equals HEAD` semantics. Reject it outside `--changed-files` the way the other read-only flags are rejected.
2. Switch `test/SKILL.md`'s pipeline QA story selection (`:70`) to `verify.js --changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}`, so selection compares story `source_files` against the run's own branch diff.
3. Switch `test/design-gate.md:9`'s `<changed-files>` resolution to the same `--ignore-stamp` form.
4. Leave `/claude-tweaks:test affected` (test re-runs) and `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping unchanged — they keep the stamp-anchored set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stamp anchored at commit A, a later source commit B, and a bookkeeping commit C on HEAD, `verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}` still returns only C's files, and `--changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}` returns B's and C's files (the merge-base diff). Both cases are covered in `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` and/or `cli.test.js`.
- `--ignore-stamp` with no resolvable `--base`/`--integration-branch` base exits 1 with a message, never an empty list.
- `--ignore-stamp` combined with a non-`--changed-files` mode is a usage error (exit 2), covered by `args.test.js`.
- `test/SKILL.md`'s QA selection and `design-gate.md` both name the `--ignore-stamp` form; the `affected` mode does not.
- The existing `verify` suites (`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/*.test.js`) pass.

## Release Note

Select pipeline QA stories against the run's full branch diff, so a build's own UI changes are never skipped because a verification stamp was written before them.

## Technical Approach

An additive flag keeps every existing `--changed-files` caller's behavior unchanged. Flipping the default would change the `affected`/`--scope` semantics that rely on the stamp anchor. The alternative of passing `--base $(git merge-base …)` from the skill prose was rejected: that hand-rolls merge-base resolution (`preferOriginRef`, degenerate-base handling) that `resolveBase` already owns.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — parse and validate `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — pass the flag through `changedFilesMode`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` — `resolveBase` skips the stamp anchor when asked
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — QA story selection uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md` — design-gate changed-file set uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` — stamp-anchored vs ignore-stamp base cases
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/args.test.js` — flag validation

## Gotchas

- `verify.js`'s usage string (`args.js:14`) and `verification.md`'s `--changed-files` description must name the new flag. Grep for every `--changed-files` mention in `plugin/skills/` before finishing (`test/SKILL.md`, `test/design-gate.md`, `test/verification.md`).
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/snippet-conformance.test.js` does not currently pin the `--changed-files` snippet. Run the full `npm test` anyway, because other conformance suites pin `test/SKILL.md` prose repo-wide.
- The reporter's alternative base (the run's materialize commit's parent) was not chosen. The integration-branch merge-base is already resolvable by `verify.js` without run-dir knowledge, and on a pr-first branch it is the same diff.

## Original request

test: pipeline QA story selection reads only post-stamp changes, so it can skip the build's own UI change

**Component:** claude-tweaks `skills/test` (pipeline QA selection) + `bin/verify.js --changed-files`
**Kind:** gap

## What happened

Inside a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the verification pass stamp. `/stories` then commits a new story YAML, and `/test` (with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present) selects stories by `source_files ∩ verify.js --changed-files`. Because `--changed-files` resolves its base to the stamp's `fullSha` whenever that sha is an ancestor of HEAD, the set at that point is only the post-stamp commits — here a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in that one-file set, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components.

## Expected

The pipeline's QA selection should compare story `source_files` against the run's own change set (the branch diff from its merge-base / the run's materialize base), not against "changes since the last verification stamp", which in a pipeline is almost always just the bookkeeping that follows `/build`.

## Workaround used

Selected stories manually against the branch diff (`git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`) and logged the deviation to `decisions.md`.

## Suggested fix

Give `/test`'s pipeline selection its own base (the run's materialize commit's parent, or `--integration-branch` merge-base) instead of the stamp-anchored `--changed-files`, or add a `--since-base` mode to `verify.js --changed-files` that ignores the stamp.


_Filed from a recommender-system `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` run (record #1207, plugin 6.136.0)._

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3048

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review`'s Step 6.7 (Late Findings Routing, `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:327`) consolidates the actionable findings from Steps 6, 6.5, 6.6, 6.65 and 6.66 into one table. Under a pipeline run it routes each finding by the resolved `review-auto-apply-ceiling` (`code-mode-steps.md:340`, `step3-routing.md`'s ceiling-keyed table). At `medium`, Low and Medium findings auto-apply as fix commits (`_shared/policy-schema.md:192`). Step 6.7 then folds each finding into its Step 7 summary section (`code-mode-steps.md:343`). It runs no QA story re-run, and nothing records that QA ran before those fixes.

`/claude-tweaks:test` ran the record's QA stories earlier in the pipeline. The QA line in `review-summary-template.md:53-61` (`### QA Validation (from /test)`, statuses ALL PASSED / PASSED WITH OBSERVATIONS / …) reports that earlier result with no freshness qualifier. The infrastructure to re-run only affected stories already exists. `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected` (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:44`) selects stories whose `source_files` intersect `verify.js --changed-files`, and stories carry a mandatory `source_files` array (`plugin/skills/stories/source-aware-design.md:66`).

Observed (reporter, 6.136.0): a single-record `auto` `/flow` run on a web UI record with `review-auto-apply-ceiling: medium`. Step 6.5 returned nine low/medium design findings, and Step 6.7 auto-applied them as nine commits that changed behaviour the passing stories describe (tooltip placement, focus/scroll after paging, a new pending state). One story's `verify` text was edited by the wave. Types/lint/tests/e2e were re-verified, but the QA stories were not re-run. The summary still read "QA: all passed" for a UI ten commits old, and the controller re-ran the stories by hand.

## Deliverables

1. In `code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7, after the resolved fixes are applied: when any applied fix touched a file listed in a QA story's `source_files`, re-run those stories via `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected` (scoped to the fix wave's changed files), and fold the result into the Step 7 QA line.
2. In `review-summary-template.md`'s QA Validation section, add a freshness qualifier for the case where QA was not re-run after an applied fix wave touching story `source_files` (for example when no dev server or browser is available): `{status} — ran before the review's fix wave ({N} commits since); stories touching changed files: {ids}`.
3. Apply the same rule to fixes applied interactively through Step 6.7's batch table ("Fix now"), not only auto-applied ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 names the post-wave re-run of affected QA stories via `/claude-tweaks:test qa affected`, gated on an applied fix touching any story's `source_files`.
- When no applied fix touches any story's `source_files`, Step 6.7 runs no QA re-run (no added cost for non-UI waves).
- `review-summary-template.md` documents the stale-QA qualifier and when it renders (applied wave touched story `source_files` and the re-run did not happen).
- The verdict comment's QA reporting reads the same qualified status (no separate wording).
- `code-mode-steps.md` stays under the per-file byte ceiling (`CEILING_BYTES`, `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js:31`), and `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Re-run affected QA stories after review auto-applies UI fixes, so the review summary never reports QA results for a UI that has since changed.

## Technical Approach

Prefer re-running over annotating. `test qa affected` already does the story selection, so the re-run reuses an existing mode instead of adding a new staleness mechanism. The qualifier only covers the case where a re-run cannot happen. The changed-file set for the wave is the files the Step 6.7 fix commits touched. Pass it the way `test/SKILL.md`'s `affected` mode documents (`verify.js --changed-files`), so stories untouched by the wave are not re-run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 post-wave affected-story re-run
- `plugin/skills/review/review-summary-template.md` — stale-QA qualifier on the QA Validation line

## Gotchas

- `code-mode-steps.md` is 41465 B against a 46080 B ceiling. Keep the Step 6.7 addition short, or cite a sub-file, as `focus-criterion-passes.md` already does for Steps 6.6-6.66.
- Out of scope: the reporter's related idea of running `design-wrapper review` before `/test`'s QA on web-surface records. That is a pipeline step-order change with its own cost tradeoff. File it separately if wanted.
- Step 3 Routing's own fix-now path (`code-mode-steps.md:258`) runs before Steps 4-7 and can also touch UI. This record is scoped to Step 6.7's late wave, the observed case.
- In a headless run with no dev server, the re-run self-skips. The qualifier must then render rather than silently reporting the pre-wave status.

## Original request

review Step 6.7: an auto-applied fix wave changes the UI after /test's QA stories ran, and nothing marks that evidence stale

**Summary:** `/review` Step 6.7 can auto-apply a fix wave that changes rendered UI after `/test`'s QA stories ran, and nothing re-runs those stories or marks the QA result as older than the wave.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:review` (code-mode Step 6.7, late findings routing) and the `/claude-tweaks:flow` step order

**Use case:**
A single-record `/flow` run in `auto` mode on a web UI record, `review-auto-apply-ceiling: medium`.

`/test` ran the record's QA stories (all passed). `/review` Step 6.5 (the design critique and audit) then returned nine low and medium findings. Under the ceiling, Step 6.7 auto-applied all of them as a fix wave of nine commits. Those commits changed rendered behaviour the stories describe: where two tooltips open, where focus and scroll land after paging, a new pending state on a control. One story's `verify` text had to be edited by the wave to stay true.

After the wave the pipeline re-verifies types, lint, tests and e2e (scoped per `test/verification.md`), but QA stories are not re-run, and nothing in the review summary, the verdict comment or the pipeline summary says the QA result predates the wave. "QA: all passed" then describes a UI ten commits old. In the observed run the controller noticed and re-ran the affected stories by hand.

Either of these would close it:

1. When Step 6.7 auto-applies a finding that touches a file listed in any story's `source_files`, mark those stories stale and re-run them after the wave, with the same tiering `/test` uses.
2. Have the review summary's QA line say so: "ran before the review's fix wave (N commits since); stories touching changed files: ...".

Related observation: the design pass is the last source of findings in `/review`, so on a UI record its fixes land after the most expensive verification (in the observed run a full verification had to be repeated). An option to run `design-wrapper review` before `/test`'s QA on records with a web surface would put those findings in front of QA instead of behind it.

Cost in the observed run: one extra full verification and a manual QA re-run.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: backend

**Related:** #3035

## Current State

The reported incident: one branch ran `/claude-tweaks:flow` on spec A and spec B. A was built in the pipeline. B was built by running `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` directly against a plan file. The flow run was "deliberately deferring its consolidated multi-spec wrap-up until both specs finished". When B finished, the user said "merge it", and the assistant "force-closed the flow run with `hooks.js close-run` before the consolidated curation ever ran". A standalone `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` then had no single record to anchor to and "fell back to inferring context from the conversation".

Verified on `origin/main`:
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md:49-53` accepts one `#N`, or else treats the input as conversation context. `:65-74`: with no argument, it detects from commits and branch, then the conversation, then a materialized header. There is no multi-record or mixed-execution case.
- `wrap-up/SKILL.md:123` and `:171`: under `MULTISPEC_CURATION_DEFER=1`, the per-spec Reflect and engine passes are skipped entirely. `:239`: under `MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER=1`, the per-spec console is skipped. The only thing that performs that deferred work is the parent run's consolidated pass (`plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md:15-19`, step 0 → `multispec-batch-curation.md`). That pass fires "after every spec's pipeline reaches `/wrap-up`'s Phase 4 … (or stops at a HARD-GATE failure)".
- `plugin/bin/hooks.js:930-985` (`close-run`) flips the run to terminal. Its only advisory is `close-without-wrapup` (`:959-964`, from `lib/hooks/close-run-state.js:127`), which checks whether any wrap-up event was recorded. It does not check whether a deferred consolidated pass ran.
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md:31-34`: a single step argument resumes from that step onward and reads prior context from files. `:22`: the only step that re-enters a multi-spec parent run is `review-console`, and only after a Halt.
- Nothing in `flow/multi-spec.md`, `wrap-up/SKILL.md` or `docs/skill-graph.md` (the wrap-up ↔ flow row at `:616`) addresses a spec that leaves the pipeline mid-run.

## Deliverables

1. Decision (approved in brainstorming 2026-10-15, revised 2026-10-16): document a convention that uses existing mechanics only. The first-approved premise did not hold: a fresh `/claude-tweaks:flow #B test` starts its own single-spec run and never rejoins the parent multi-spec run. The convention is therefore:
   - B's own tail run (`test` onward) comes first, with its merge decision left open.
   - B is marked `not-run` in the parent manifest via `hooks.js spec-status`.
   - The parent's consolidated pass is the single merge.
   - `close-run` comes last.

   The convention also carries the warning that closing the parent first forfeits the deferred consolidated wrap-up, which is what lost it in the incident. Rejected: declaring mixed execution unsupported, because it strands real mixed runs. Rejected: a `#A,#B` wrap-up mode, a second consolidation path beside `/flow`'s multi-spec console. **Blocked by #3035:** `hooks.js spec-status` refuses today because no CLI creates `manifest.yml`, so step (c) below can't run until #3035 ships.
2. Add a `## Mixed execution (a spec built outside /flow)` section to `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md`. This is the canonical home. It must state:
   - (a) A spec implemented outside the pipeline rejoins at `test` via `/claude-tweaks:flow #B test`. Cite the resume grammar from `steps-and-gates.md`'s Step Arguments rather than restating it.
   - (b) That invocation is its own single-spec run with its own wrap-up and Review Console. It does not feed the parent run's consolidated console.
   - (c) The parent run's spec B is recorded `not-run` through `hooks.js spec-status` (the manifest's only writer), so the consolidated console's Not run / Failed footer names it.
   - (d) The warning: the parent run's deferred consolidated pass must run before `close-run` on the parent. Closing first forfeits Reflect, the curation engine and the console for every spec that ran under `MULTISPEC_CURATION_DEFER=1`, because their per-spec passes were skipped (cite `wrap-up/SKILL.md`'s defer branches) and nothing else performs them.
   - (e) The order:
     1. B's tail run, with its merge decision left open.
     2. The parent's consolidated pass, whose terminal decision is the run's single merge. This is `multispec-review-console.md`'s "Approve all + merge"; "Approve all, leave PR open" defers the merge to a human.
     3. `close-run` last.
3. Add a one-sentence pointer to the new section in `wrap-up/SKILL.md`'s "If no arguments, detect from context" block. It covers the case where two records share one branch, or one record's run is already closed. Do not restate the convention there.
4. Update the wrap-up ↔ flow row in `docs/skill-graph.md` (`:616`) to name the mixed-execution convention as part of that existing edge.
5. Add a conformance test pinning the new prose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New `tests/flow-mixed-execution-convention.test.js`:
  - `multi-spec.md` has the `## Mixed execution` heading. Its section contains `/claude-tweaks:flow #`, `test`, `close-run`, `not-run` and `MULTISPEC_CURATION_DEFER`, and cites `steps-and-gates.md`.
  - `wrap-up/SKILL.md`'s detect-from-context block contains a pointer naming `multi-spec.md`'s Mixed execution section.
  - The wrap-up section of `docs/skill-graph.md` mentions mixed execution.
- [ ] Each new assertion is shown to go red against `origin/main`'s text (revert-to-prove-red, per the skill-prose-conformance-tests skill).
- [ ] The section uses the fully qualified `/claude-tweaks:flow` form in its instruction text.
- [ ] `npm test` passes, including the context-cost composed and raw gates for `wrap-up/SKILL.md` and `flow/multi-spec.md`.

## Release Note

Document how a spec built outside /flow rejoins the pipeline, and warn that closing a multi-spec run before its consolidated wrap-up loses that wrap-up.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/flow/multi-spec.md`: new Mixed execution section, the canonical statement.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md`: one-line pointer in the detect-from-context block.
- `docs/skill-graph.md`: extends the wrap-up ↔ flow edge row.
- `tests/flow-mixed-execution-convention.test.js` (new): the prose pins.

## Gotchas

- `/claude-tweaks:flow #B test` started fresh is a separate single-spec run. Under `pr-first` its wrap-up reaches a merge decision for the shared branch/PR, so the section must tell the reader to leave that one open. The parent console's Shared teardown removes the shared worktree (`multispec-review-console.md:182`), which is why B's tail goes first. Trace both against `steps-and-gates.md`'s adoption cases and `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` before writing.
- The consolidated batch pass scopes its diff from the merge-base with the integration branch (`multispec-batch-curation.md:24`), so B's commits on the shared branch fall inside it. B's own wrap-up then routes overlapping learnings. Name this duplication in the section rather than leaving it implicit.
- Do not describe `close-run`'s `close-without-wrapup` advisory as a guard here. It checks for any wrap-up event and is not specific to the deferred consolidated pass.
- `wrap-up/SKILL.md` is about 36 KB. Keep the pointer to one sentence and measure `wc -c` plus the composed bytes before adding it.

## Original request

wrap-up: no convention for a branch that mixes /flow orchestration with direct subagent-driven-development execution

**Summary:** When one branch builds part of a multi-spec batch through `/claude-tweaks:flow` and another part through `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` run directly, wrap-up's record-identity detection and the multi-spec consolidated wrap-up have no defined way to compose the two.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** /claude-tweaks:wrap-up (record-identity detection) and /claude-tweaks:flow multi-spec consolidated wrap-up ([MULTISPEC_CURATION_DEFER]/[MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER])

**Use case:**
In a private project, a single feature branch (one PR) ran `/claude-tweaks:flow` on two specs, spec A and spec B. Spec A was built inside the flow pipeline, but spec B was implemented by running `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` directly against a plan file, outside the pipeline. The flow run was deliberately deferring its consolidated multi-spec wrap-up until both specs finished. When spec B's direct execution finished, the user said "merge it", and the assistant force-closed the flow run with `hooks.js close-run` before the consolidated curation ever ran. `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up` was then invoked standalone with no single record identity to anchor to (two records, one PR, one record's run already closed), so it fell back to inferring context from the conversation.

Nothing in the plugin says which of these is the intended behaviour:
(a) every spec in a combined /flow run must stay inside /flow — dropping to direct SDD mid-run is unsupported;
(b) /flow accepts a spec whose implementation happened via direct SDD and folds it into the same consolidated wrap-up;
(c) mixed execution is normal, and wrap-up's record-identity detection gains an explicit multi-record / mixed-execution case instead of falling back to conversation context.

**Definition:** Needed — three viable directions (a/b/c) with no tradeoff chosen yet.

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2677, #2776, #2882, #3001, #3003, #3004, #3013, #3014, #3060

## Current State

In a pipeline run, the ephemeral dev/prod server that QA and `/claude-tweaks:visual-review` use is started detached and recorded in `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt` as `{pid} {port} {worktree-root} detached:{yes|no}` (`plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md:135`). It stays up until `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s Section D cleanup, which reads the file's *current* content under the liveness-handle rule, because a later step may have restarted the server and rewritten it (`dev-url-detection.md:171-176`).

`/claude-tweaks:review`'s fix paths rebuild the app under that live server without coordinating with it:

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md:114`: "If any findings are 'Fix now', make the changes, re-verify per `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s Re-verification rule (`/claude-tweaks:test`)…"
- `step3-routing.md:116-120`, Parallel fix dispatch (3+ independent fixes): dispatches fix agents, then re-runs `/claude-tweaks:test`.
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:327` Step 6.7 (Late Findings Routing) applies AUTO-routed design, visual and security findings through the same routing.

Neither file mentions the ephemeral server, and the fix-agent dispatch prompt has no "do not build or start servers" line. A project rule forbidding builds under a live server binds only the orchestrating session, never a fix agent the plugin dispatches.

Observed (plugin 6.136.0, `/claude-tweaks:flow` on a private Next.js 16 app): review Step 6.7 AUTO-applied four visual and design findings. The fixer's verification ran the project's e2e suite, whose `next build` rewrote `.next` in the shared worktree. Meanwhile the run's ephemeral `next start` (pid in `ephemeral-server.txt`) was still serving that directory to QA and visual review. Nothing failed loudly. The server sat on a replaced build.

## Deliverables

1. In `step3-routing.md`'s fix path, sequential and parallel alike (and therefore Step 6.7), add a step before re-verify or fix-agent dispatch: when `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt` names a live server whose worktree is this checkout, stop it first.
2. After re-verify, if a later step still needs a browser (visual review, QA re-runs), restart the server through `dev-url-detection.md`'s ephemeral start. Rewrite `ephemeral-server.txt` with a plain Bash redirect under the existing liveness-handle rule, so Section D kills the current pid. When no later step needs a browser, leave the server stopped and remove the stale line so Section D does not try to kill a dead pid.
3. Add a line to the fix-agent dispatch prompt: "do not run the project's builds, test suites or servers; the dispatcher re-verifies."
4. Add one sentence to `dev-url-detection.md`'s Cleanup section: an in-pipeline step that rebuilds the served app must stop and later restart the server. Point to the review step that does this.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a pipeline review that applies a fix and re-verifies with a suite that builds the app, no later step is served by a process running a replaced build. The server was stopped before the build and, when still needed, restarted after it with a new pid in `ephemeral-server.txt`.
- Wrap-up's Section D still kills the server that is current at end of run, with no orphan left from before the restart.
- The fix-agent prompt template carries the no-build/no-server line. A conformance test pins it together with the stop and restart step in `step3-routing.md`, and goes red against the current text.
- A standalone review (no run dir, so no `ephemeral-server.txt`) behaves exactly as today.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Code review's fixes no longer rebuild your app underneath the test server the pipeline is still using. The server is stopped and restarted around the rebuild.

## Technical Approach

Stop/restart is chosen over isolating the build output. Build output paths are framework-specific (`.next`, `dist`, `build`), and the plugin cannot redirect them generically without project config. The server lifecycle, by contrast, is already the plugin's own (`ephemeral-server.txt`, the liveness-handle rule, Section D). Reuse the existing ephemeral start/stop procedures from `dev-url-detection.md`; never hand-roll a kill. The fix-agent prompt line keeps verification with the dispatcher, so only one place has to coordinate with the server.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — Fix-now re-verify (`:114`) and Parallel fix dispatch (`:116-120`) gain the stop/restart step and the fix-agent prompt line
- `plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` — Step 6.7 (`:327`) inherits it through the routing; confirm no separate re-verify path bypasses it
- `plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` — Cleanup section (`:171-176`) gains the rebuild-under-server sentence
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/cleanup-procedures.md` — reference for Section D's read of the current `ephemeral-server.txt`; not modified unless the stale-line case needs handling

## Gotchas

- #3001 (ready) adds a no-suites/no-servers rule for Step 3's read-only *lens* agents. This record covers the *fix* path, where building is legitimate but uncoordinated. Keep the two prompt lines consistent in wording, and do not merge them into one rule that would forbid the dispatcher's own re-verify.
- `ephemeral-server.txt`'s worktree field must match this checkout before stopping anything. A sibling run's server on another worktree must never be killed.
- Rewriting `ephemeral-server.txt` must go through a plain Bash redirect from the main checkout's run dir (`_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md`, `[IL-127]`). A worktree-relative path would shadow it and leave Section D killing the old pid.
- A restart costs a cold start. Do it once after the whole fix batch re-verifies, not per finding.

## Original request

review: a fix's re-verify rebuilds the app under the run's still-live ephemeral server, and nothing in the fix path reads `ephemeral-server.txt`

**Summary:** In a pipeline run, the ephemeral dev/prod server that QA and `/claude-tweaks:visual-review` use stays up until wrap-up cleanup (`_shared/dev-url-detection.md`, Cleanup: "The calling skill does not stop it mid-pipeline"). Review's fix paths re-run `/claude-tweaks:test` after applying findings, and a fix agent can run its own build. Either one can run a check that rebuilds the artifacts the live server is serving. Neither the fix path nor the fix-agent dispatch prompt reads `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt`, so the server keeps running on a build that was swapped out underneath it.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `skills/review/step3-routing.md` (the "Fix now" re-verify line and "Parallel fix dispatch"), `skills/review/code-mode-steps.md` Step 6.7 (it applies AUTO fixes through the same routing), `skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md` (Cleanup)

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

## Current State

- `dev-url-detection.md` starts the server detached, records `PID PORT WORKTREE detached:yes` in `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt`, and leaves it running until wrap-up's Section D cleanup.
- `step3-routing.md` says: "If any findings are 'Fix now', make the changes, re-verify per `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s Re-verification rule (`/claude-tweaks:test`)". Its parallel fix dispatch then re-runs `/claude-tweaks:test` after the diff audit. Step 6.7 applies its AUTO-routed design and visual findings through these same rules.
- Neither file mentions the ephemeral server, and the fix-agent output template has no "do not build or start servers" line.
- A project can forbid builds under a live server (the reporting project's rules file does, and so does the user's memory). That only binds the orchestrating session's own commands. It never reaches a fix agent the plugin dispatches, and the plugin's own re-verify does not consult it either.

**Observed (plugin 6.136.0, `/claude-tweaks:flow` on a private project's Next.js 16 app):** review Step 6.7 AUTO-applied four visual and design findings. The fixer's verification ran the project's e2e suite, whose `next build` rewrote `.next` in the shared worktree. Meanwhile the run's ephemeral `next start` was still serving that directory to QA and visual review, with its pid recorded in `ephemeral-server.txt`. Nothing failed loudly; the server simply sat on a replaced build. The run had already flagged the same hazard as latent on an earlier record. This time it was observed.

**Related, not a duplicate:** #3001 covers Step 3's read-only *lens* agents running the e2e suite during the fan-out. This issue covers the *fix* path, where building is legitimate (re-verification is required) but is not coordinated with the run's live server.

## Deliverables

1. In `step3-routing.md`'s fix path, both sequential and parallel (and therefore Step 6.7), add a step before re-verify or fix-agent dispatch: when `{run-dir}/ephemeral-server.txt` names a live server whose worktree is this checkout, stop it first. Alternatively, have the build write somewhere other than the directory the server serves.
2. After re-verify, if any later step still needs a browser (visual review, QA re-runs), restart the server through `dev-url-detection.md`'s ephemeral start. Rewrite `ephemeral-server.txt` with a plain Bash redirect under the existing liveness-handle rule, so wrap-up cleanup kills the right pid.
3. Add a line to the fix-agent dispatch prompt that keeps verification with the dispatcher: "do not run the project's builds, test suites or servers; the dispatcher re-verifies."
4. Add one sentence to `dev-url-detection.md`'s Cleanup section: an in-pipeline step that rebuilds the served app must stop and later restart the server, and should point to the review step that does this.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a pipeline review that applies a fix and re-verifies with a suite that builds the app, no step that follows is served by a process running on a replaced build. Either the server was stopped before the build and restarted after it, with a new pid in `ephemeral-server.txt`, or the build wrote to an isolated output.
- Wrap-up's Section D cleanup still kills the server that is current at end-of-run, with no orphan left from before the restart.
- The fix-agent prompt template carries the no-build/no-server line, and a contract test pins it together with the stop and restart step in `step3-routing.md`.
- A standalone review (no run dir, so no `ephemeral-server.txt`) behaves exactly as it does today.

**Definition:** Clear

Surface: backend

**Related:** #2956, #3017

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3 builds one shared context bundle and hands its path to every lens agent. The bundle has no size bound. Reported: a 32-file feature diff gave `bytes` 1,970,636 with `emptySections` empty, and a follow-up comment on 6.138.0 reports a 1,274,411-byte bundle (16 files) where one file was a ~900 KB captured-API `.jsonl` fixture. In both cases the controller dropped the bundle and gave agents the file list instead, a path the dispatch contract does not describe. `--files-from` is the only escape hatch today.

Verified on `origin/main`:
- `plugin/bin/lib/review-context/build.js:64-75`: `buildContext` appends `===== {f} =====` and the file's whole working-tree content for every in-scope file, whatever its size. The only degraded case is a failed read, which goes into `emptySections`.
- `build.js:79`: returns `{ dir, contextPath, bytes, files, emptySections }`. `bytes` is computed but nothing ever checks it.
- `build.js:39-43`: the module's own comment already says a section can degrade safely because "the full diff at the top still carries that file's change". This is the same argument a stub section relies on.
- `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js:74-75` prints that object as one JSON line. Lines 6-7 of the header comment list its fields.
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md:68` documents the printed line as `{dir, contextPath, bytes, files, emptySections}`, and `:70` explains `emptySections`. `docs/plugin-structure.md:189` repeats the same field list.
- `tests/bin-lib/review-context/build.test.js` covers the bundle shape (line 69) and the CLI end to end (line 118). It has no size case.

## Deliverables

1. Decision (approved in brainstorming, 2026-10-15): cap each file's section. A file's full content is inlined only when it is under a per-file cap of 64 KB, held in a named exported constant. Larger files get a stub section instead, because the full diff at the top of the bundle already carries their hunks. Stubbed files are listed in a new `oversizeSections` field of the printed JSON line. Lockfiles and `*.jsonl` are always stubbed. The design keeps the single `contextPath` that every lens prompt relies on. Rejected: excluding generated files only, because it gives no general bound and any large hand-written file still floods the bundle. Rejected: splitting the bundle per file with an index, because it changes every consumer of `contextPath`.
2. `build.js`: add an exported constant, `PER_FILE_CAP_BYTES = 64 * 1024`, and an exported always-stub matcher. The matcher covers `*.jsonl` and named lockfiles (at least `package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `composer.lock`), matched on basename.
3. `buildContext`:
   - A file the matcher catches gets a stub without being read.
   - Other files are read as now. When content is over the cap (measured with `Buffer.byteLength`), the full content is replaced by a one-line stub that gives the file's byte size and points to the diff above and to reading the live file.
   - Push each stubbed path to `oversizeSections`, in file order, and add the field to the return value.
   - A failed read still goes to `emptySections` and never to `oversizeSections`.
4. CLI header comment, `step3-lens-dispatch.md:68-70` and `docs/plugin-structure.md:189`: name `oversizeSections` in the printed field list. In `step3-lens-dispatch.md`, add one sentence beside the `emptySections` paragraph saying stubbed sections degrade the same way, and that the lens reads the live file when it needs the full content.
5. **Diff block (extension approved 2026-10-16).** Apply the same rule to the diff at the top of the bundle. An added or deleted file whose hunk text exceeds `PER_FILE_CAP_BYTES`, or any always-stub match (lockfile or `*.jsonl`), has its hunk replaced by one marker line, `[{N} bytes of diff elided for {path} — see oversizeSections]`. Its path joins `oversizeSections`. A *modified* file's hunks stay whole, since they are the review's subject. Split the diff per file on the `diff --git` headers git emits, rather than re-running git per file.
6. Tests in `tests/bin-lib/review-context/build.test.js` (see Acceptance Criteria).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build.test.js`: a fixture file of `PER_FILE_CAP_BYTES + 1` bytes gets a stub section. Its full content is absent from `context.md`, its path appears in `oversizeSections`, and its hunk is still present in the diff part of the bundle.
- [ ] `build.test.js`: a file of exactly `PER_FILE_CAP_BYTES` bytes is inlined in full and is not listed.
- [ ] `build.test.js`: a small `fixture.jsonl` and a small `package-lock.json` are both stubbed and listed in `oversizeSections`, despite being under the cap.
- [ ] `build.test.js`: a deleted file still lands in `emptySections` only, and the existing `deepStrictEqual(result.emptySections, ['doomed.txt'])` assertions still pass.
- [ ] `build.test.js` CLI end-to-end test: the parsed JSON line has an `oversizeSections` array.
- [ ] `build.test.js`: a newly *added* file over the cap, and an added small `fixture.jsonl`, each have their diff hunk replaced by the single `bytes of diff elided` marker line, and appear in `oversizeSections` once each (not twice). A *modified* file over the cap keeps its full hunk in the diff block.
- [ ] `step3-lens-dispatch.md` and `docs/plugin-structure.md` both contain `oversizeSections`, pinned by a new assertion in `tests/bin-lib/review-context/prose.test.js`.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Cap each file in /review's shared lens bundle at 64 KB and always stub lockfiles and `.jsonl`, so lens agents can read the bundle on ordinary feature diffs.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files
- `plugin/bin/lib/review-context/build.js`: adds the cap constant and the always-stub matcher, adds stub sections in `buildContext`, and adds `oversizeSections` to the return value.
- `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js`: updates the header comment's field list. The JSON line passes the result through unchanged.
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`: updates the printed-line field list at :68 and adds the stub-degradation sentence next to :70.
- `docs/plugin-structure.md`: updates the field list at :189.
- `tests/bin-lib/review-context/build.test.js`: adds the cap, boundary, always-stub and CLI-field cases.
- `tests/bin-lib/review-context/prose.test.js`: pins `oversizeSections` in both prose files.

## Gotchas

- Deliverable 5 bounds added and deleted files' diff hunks, but a *modified* file's hunks are deliberately left whole, so a huge rewrite of an existing file can still make `bytes` large. No prose may claim the whole bundle is strictly bounded. `--files-from` remains the escape hatch.
- Dedupe `oversizeSections`: a file stubbed in both the diff block and its own section is listed once.
- The stub line must not look like file content. Lens agents report `Path:Line` from the live file (`step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s file-native rule), so keep the stub to one clearly marked line.
- Keep `readFile` as the only file seam, because the tests inject it to anchor paths to the fixture repo (`build.test.js:38-43`). Measure size from the content that was read rather than adding a `stat` call the fake does not provide.
- Check the name matcher before reading, so a deleted lockfile counts as stubbed rather than empty. State that order in a code comment.

## Original request

build-review-context.js: the shared review bundle has no size bound and is unreadable on an ordinary feature diff

**Summary:** `build-review-context.js build` writes one context file holding the full diff plus every changed file in full, with no size bound; on a 32-file feature diff it came out at about 1.97 MB, far more than a dispatched lens agent can read, so the bundle that `step3-lens-dispatch.md` tells the controller to hand to every lens went unused.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `bin/build-review-context.js` (and `skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`, which hands its output path to every lens agent)

**Repro steps:**
1. On a feature branch whose diff includes a few large files (here: an implementation plan of about 940 lines and several test files of a few thousand lines each, 32 changed files in all), run `node bin/build-review-context.js build --base <base> --branch HEAD --run <run-dir>`.
2. Read the printed JSON line: `bytes` was 1,970,636 for `files` 32, with `emptySections` empty.
3. Follow `step3-lens-dispatch.md` and give each lens agent the bundle path as its shared context.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a bundle a lens agent can read in one or two calls, or a build that reports the bundle is too large and says what to hand the agents instead (for example the diff alone, or one file per changed path with an index).
Actual: the build succeeds silently at any size. A lens agent handed a 2 MB file must page through it in many reads, most of it unchanged test code, before it reaches the hunks; the controller's practical choice is to drop the bundle and give each agent the file list and the diff scope, which the dispatch contract does not describe.

**Definition:** Needed — either cap and degrade (diff plus changed hunks with context, full files only below a size bound), or split the bundle per file with an index. The size bound itself is an open choice.

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

`liftMetadata` in `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js:119-138` lifts a record's body-metadata lines into the materialized header. The `Design-intent:` capture is `/^Design-intent:[ \t]*(\S+)/m` (`:131`). `\S+` stops at the first whitespace, so `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` lifts as `quiet,` (trailing comma kept, second value lost). `composeHeader` (`:157-169`) then writes `design-intent: quiet,` verbatim.

Multi-value intents are a supported shape downstream. `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md:106` says "Multiple intents (comma-separated, e.g., `design-intent: bold, delightful`) trigger multiple dispatches." Polish reads the header's `design-intent:` for that dispatch, and so do `flow/manifesto.md:43` and `:57`. The run-level lever is a single-value enum in `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js:95` (`none | bold | quiet | minimal | delightful | onboarding`).

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), the header read `design-intent: quiet,` and `config.yml` resolved to `quiet` only. Polish ran the `minimal` command only because the polish agent happened to re-read the record body. A mechanical header consumer would have skipped it.

## Deliverables

1. Change `liftMetadata`'s `Design-intent:` capture to the full same-line value: split on `,`, trim each value, drop empties, and validate each against the closed enum from `policy-schema.js:95` (read from there, not re-listed). The lifted value is a normalized list.
2. `composeHeader` writes the normalized list as `design-intent: quiet, minimal` (comma plus single space), the shape `command-map.md:106` documents. A single value is written exactly as today.
3. An unknown value (outside the enum), or a list that mixes `none` with any other value, fails materialization with a message naming the record and the offending value, the same hard-gate posture as other malformed header input. It never silently drops the value.
4. Decide how a multi-value header maps to the run-level `design-intent` lever, which is single-valued in `policy-schema.js`. Either have polish read the header list (not the lever) for dispatch, or document in `flow/manifesto.md` that the lever is a run default and the header list is authoritative per record. Pick one, and make the manifesto's Design-intent row (`manifesto.md:57`) state it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test lifts `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` and asserts the header line `design-intent: quiet, minimal`. Prove it goes red against the current `\S+` capture.
- Unit tests cover: a single value (unchanged output); extra spaces and a trailing comma (`quiet ,minimal,` → `quiet, minimal`); an unknown value (materialization fails, naming it); `none, bold` (fails).
- A bare `Design-intent:` line with no value still lifts nothing. The existing refs-#357 same-line-only behavior is pinned by an unchanged test.
- The polish dispatch path receives both intents for a two-value header, asserted by a test or conformance check on whichever consumer Deliverable 4 picks.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Records with more than one design intent now carry every intent into the build, so polish runs each one instead of only the first.

## Technical Approach

Keep the change local to `liftMetadata`/`composeHeader`. Capture with `(.+)$` like `Ui-stack:` already does at `:133`, keeping the `[ \t]*` same-line guard, then normalize. Source the enum from `policy-schema.js` so the two cannot drift. Hard-fail on invalid values rather than filtering: a silent drop is the exact failure this record reports, one level down.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js` — `liftMetadata` `Design-intent:` capture (`:131-132`), list normalization and validation; `composeHeader` output (`:169`)
- `plugin/bin/lib/policy-schema.js` — enum source of truth (`:95`), read not modified
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — Design-intent lever vs. per-record header list (`:43`, `:57`)
- `plugin/skills/design-wrapper/command-map.md` — reference for the documented multi-intent shape (`:106`)

## Gotchas

- The refs-#357 comment at `materialize-format.js:124-128` explains why every capture uses `[ \t]*`, not `\s*`. Keep that guard on the new capture, or a bare `Design-intent:` line will swallow the next line.
- `yamlSafeScalar` (`:146`) is applied only to `ui-stack`. A comma-separated list contains no `:` or `#`, so it needs no quoting, but do not route it through a YAML-list syntax that other header readers do not parse.
- Records already materialized with `design-intent: quiet,` live in old run dirs. Readers must not crash on that legacy shape. Treat a trailing comma as a trimmed list on read too, if any reader re-parses the header.

## Original request

materialize.js: a comma-separated `Design-intent:` list is truncated to its first value

**Summary:** `materialize.js` lifts `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` into the materialized header as `design-intent: quiet,` — trailing comma kept, second value lost.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/materialize.js, bin/lib/issues/materialize-format.js (`liftMetadata`)

**Repro steps:**
1. Create a record whose body carries `Design-intent: quiet, minimal` (what `/claude-tweaks:specify` writes when two intents are picked).
2. Run `/claude-tweaks:flow #N` (or `bin/materialize.js` directly) to materialize it.
3. Read the materialized header in `{run-dir}/work/{n}-spec.md` and the run's `config.yml` `design-intent` lever.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: the whole list is lifted (`design-intent: quiet, minimal`, or a YAML list), or each value is validated against the closed enum (`bold | quiet | minimal | delightful | onboarding | none`) and malformed input fails the materialization gate.
Actual: the header reads `design-intent: quiet,` and `config.yml` resolves to `quiet` only. The polish phase still ran the `minimal` intent's command only because the polish agent re-read the record body; a mechanical consumer of the header would have skipped it.

Suggested fix: capture the full same-line value, split on `,`, trim, validate against the enum, emit a normalized list; add a test for a two-value intent line.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

## Current State

The SubagentStop hook (`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js`) grades a dispatched subagent's reply against the Subagent Contract: the last non-empty line must read `STATUS: {DONE|DONE_WITH_CONCERNS|NEEDS_CONTEXT|BLOCKED}` (`CANONICAL_RE`), and a non-compliant reply is blocked and retried in-run.

A subagent running `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3's lens fan-out launched 8 in-turn `Agent` dispatches and yielded with a one-line progress note while 5 were still pending — the pattern the dispatch prompt sanctions, since the harness delivers the completions back into the same turn sequence. The hook graded that progress note as the final reply and blocked, forcing the subagent to emit a `STATUS:` line mid-run, before its review, polish, and wrap-up work had run. A dispatcher reading that first `STATUS:` line would treat an unfinished run as complete. Reported on plugin 6.136.0.

Two partial mitigations already exist and did not cover this case:

- #2041's `asyncWaitCheckpoint`: skips grading only when the reply immediately follows an async signal in the transcript (`isAsyncWaitSignal`: an `isAsync: true` Agent launch result, or a `task-notification`). A yield composed after other tool calls has no such signal right before it.
- #2714's `INTERIM_STATUS:` marker (`isInterimProgressReply`): an opt-in trailing line that exempts a reply. It works only when the dispatch prompt tells the subagent to use it; only `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` and `reflect/full-mode.md` mention it, and review's lens fan-out does not.

Neither knows whether the subagent still has dispatches outstanding.

## Deliverables

1. The hook counts the subagent's own in-turn `Agent` dispatches that are still pending at the time of the reply — async launches seen in its transcript minus completions delivered as task notifications — and skips grading (or logs it as advisory only) while that count is above zero.
2. A reply with nothing pending is graded exactly as today, including the existing #2041 and #2714 exemptions.
3. Transcript parsing stays defensive: an unparseable or unexpected shape falls back to today's grading, never to a blanket exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A transcript fixture where a subagent launched async `Agent` dispatches and yields before all completions arrive is not blocked and is not forced to emit a `STATUS:` line.
2. A transcript fixture where every launched dispatch has completed, ending in a non-compliant reply, is still blocked.
3. A reply ending in `INTERIM_STATUS:` and a reply right after an async signal behave as today.
4. The fixtures are taken from a real transcript's line shapes, not invented; the hook's existing tests pass.

## Release Note

Subagents that pause while their own background agents are still running are no longer forced to report a final status early.

## Technical Approach

Extend the transcript scan `subagent-stop.js` already performs (`lastAssistantText`, `isAsyncWaitSignal`) to collect launched async dispatch ids (from the Agent tool result) and completed ids (from task-notification entries), then exempt the reply while any launched id lacks a completion. Correlate by id rather than by count where the transcript carries one.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` — pending-dispatch count and exemption
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — note that pending in-turn dispatches exempt a yield, beside the `INTERIM_STATUS:` rule
- `tests/bin-lib/hooks/contract-retries.test.js` — existing SubagentStop coverage; add the new fixtures
- `docs/hooks.md` — SubagentStop behavior description

## Gotchas

- Confirm the transcript field shapes (async launch result id, task-notification payload) against a live transcript before writing the parser; #2041's own comment notes its shapes were verified that way.
- A dispatch that never completes would exempt the subagent forever; bound the exemption (for example, only while the launch is newer than the reply, or a ceiling on the number of exempted stops) so a hung child cannot hide a real contract violation.
- Adding the `INTERIM_STATUS:` instruction to review's lens fan-out prompt would also fix the reported run, but leaves every other nested dispatcher exposed; the mechanical count is the general fix, and the prompt instruction can be a follow-up.

## Original request

SubagentStop contract check fires on an intermediate yield while in-turn Agent completions are still pending

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** bin/hooks.js subagent-stop (Subagent Contract STATUS-line check)

## Current State

A dispatched subagent ran review Step 3's lens fan-out: 8 in-turn `Agent` reproduction-pair dispatches. It yielded briefly with a one-line progress note while 5 completions were still pending. That yield is the pattern the dispatch prompt explicitly sanctions: the harness delivers the completion notifications back into the same turn sequence. The `subagent-stop` hook treated the progress note as the subagent's final reply. It then blocked with "your reply's last non-empty line must read exactly STATUS: ...". To get past it, the subagent had to emit a `STATUS:` line mid-run, before the review, polish and wrap-up phases had run. A dispatcher that reads the first stop's STATUS line would take an unfinished run as complete.

## Deliverables

- Make the subagent-stop check aware of outstanding in-turn Agent dispatches, e.g. by tracking launched vs completed task notifications for the session. Skip the contract check, or downgrade it to advisory, while any are pending.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A subagent that yields while its own in-turn Agent dispatches are still running is not forced to emit a STATUS line.
- A subagent that yields with nothing pending is still held to the contract, as today.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2775, #2783, #2868, #2912, #2914, #2994, #3003, #3012, #3132

## Current State

When `/claude-tweaks:flow` adopts an inherited run directory, as `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s second call (`review,polish,wrap-up`) does, it gathers facts once via `bin/flow-preflight.js` (`plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md:56-60`). The pack's `pr` probe (`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js:263-268`) runs `gh pr view {n} --json state,isDraft,body` and returns `{number, url, branch, state, isDraft, checklist}`. It never reads `mergeable` or `mergeStateStatus`.

In the reported run (plugin 6.136.0), the integration branch moved between the two dispatch calls. A sibling PR edited the same two lines of two skill docs, so the run's PR became `CONFLICTING`. GitHub runs no `pull_request` CI on a conflicting PR, so the checks list held only the label workflow. The second call's verification stamp and the first call's decisions log both read green. The conflict surfaced only because the reviewer ran an ad-hoc `gh pr view --json mergeable`. Nothing in the pack, the adoption path, or `/review` Step 1.5 (`plugin/skills/review/code-mode-steps.md:57`) looks at mergeability.

## Deliverables

1. Extend the pack's `pr` probe to request `mergeable,mergeStateStatus` alongside `state,isDraft,body`, and return both fields. A forge or `gh` that omits them yields `null` for that field, never an error that fails the whole `pr` probe.
2. On the adopted-run path (`steps-and-gates.md`'s "Adopting an inherited run directory"), when the pack's `pr.mergeable` is `CONFLICTING`, print one visible line before any later phase runs: `Run PR #{n} is CONFLICTING with {integration branch} — CI will not run on it until the conflict is resolved.` Log it as an `AUTO` decision. Then reconcile per the existing catch-up procedure: merge the integration branch into the run branch, then re-verify. This is the same remedy `_shared/worktree-catchup-no-run-dir.md` and the phase-exit pushes already use. Cite the existing procedure; do not restate it.
3. When the merge in deliverable 2 itself conflicts, stop as a HARD-GATE failure with the conflicting paths named, rather than continuing to review on a stamp that no longer describes a mergeable tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test feeds the `pr` probe a `gh` stub returning `mergeable: CONFLICTING` and asserts the pack's `pr` carries `mergeable` and `mergeStateStatus`. A stub omitting both asserts `null` values and `ok: true`.
- A test or conformance assertion pins the adopted-run path's `CONFLICTING` line and its routing to the catch-up procedure. It goes red against the current `steps-and-gates.md`.
- A `MERGEABLE` or `UNKNOWN` PR produces no new line, no new decision entry, and no behavior change. A test asserts this.
- Existing `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight-cli.test.js`, and `tests/flow-preflight-conformance.test.js` pass, updated only where they pin the `pr` field's exact key set.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

A resumed pipeline run now notices when its pull request has picked up a merge conflict since the last call, and catches up before reviewing.

## Technical Approach

Keep the change inside the probe that already reads the PR. One more pair of JSON fields on the same `gh pr view` call adds no new network round-trip. The adoption-path handling is prose in `steps-and-gates.md`, keyed off the pack field, so the decision stays mechanical and is never re-derived by hand. `UNKNOWN` is GitHub's transient value while it computes mergeability, so it must stay a no-op, as the original request asks. The merge gate re-reads mergeability at merge time anyway.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js` — `pr` probe (`:263-268`) requests and returns `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus`
- `plugin/skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md` — "Adopting an inherited run directory" (`:56`) surfaces a `CONFLICTING` PR and routes to catch-up
- `tests/bin-lib/flow/preflight.test.js` — `pr` probe field assertions
- `tests/flow-preflight-conformance.test.js` — adoption-path prose pin

## Gotchas

- The pack field set may be pinned by conformance tests and consumed by other readers of `preflight.json`. Add fields; never rename or drop `state`/`isDraft`/`checklist`.
- `mergeable` is computed lazily by GitHub. A first read right after a push often returns `UNKNOWN`. Do not poll in the probe, because the pack has a probe timeout (`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `preflight.js:284`).
- #3013 (ready) adds a PR-check read to `/test` and `/review` Step 1.5. A conflicting PR has no CI, so an empty check rollup there would read as pending. These two records cover different signals. Keep the `CONFLICTING` handling on the adoption path, as this record specifies, and do not fold it into #3013's check read.

## Original request

flow-preflight's pr probe omits mergeable state, so a two-call dispatch resume misses a PR that turned CONFLICTING between calls

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** bin/flow-preflight.js (pr probe), skills/flow/steps-and-gates.md (Adopting an inherited run directory)

## Current State

On a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` two-call handoff (`build,test`, then `review,polish,wrap-up` against the same `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`), the second call's `flow-preflight.js` pack reports `pr: {number, url, branch, state, isDraft, checklist}`. It does not report `mergeable`. In one run the integration branch moved between the two calls. A sibling PR edited the same two lines of two skill docs, so the run's PR was `CONFLICTING`. The forge then ran no `pull_request` CI on it (GitHub skips CI on conflicting PRs). The second call's verification stamp and the first call's decisions log both read green. The conflict surfaced only because the reviewer ran an ad-hoc `gh pr view --json mergeable` and found just the label workflow in the checks list. Nothing in the pack or in review Step 1.5/2 checks it.

## Deliverables

- Add `mergeable` (and `mergeStateStatus` where the forge supports it) to the pack's `pr` probe.
- When it reads `CONFLICTING`, surface it on the adopted-run path, before review's test gate trusts a stamp. Either say how to reconcile (merge the integration branch in, then re-verify) or make it an explicit gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A resumed run whose PR is `CONFLICTING` prints a visible line naming the conflict before review starts.
- A `MERGEABLE` or `UNKNOWN` PR changes nothing.

**Definition:** Clear

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0

Origin: reflect light mode from #2694, lens "Friction"
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`'s bookkeeping-stamps gate (`hasClaimLogFor` /
`hasLoggedPrEarlyStep1`, and their siblings) recognizes a prior call's Step 2.8 claim or
PR-early-run-lifecycle step only by matching `decisions.md` against an exact-format regex
(e.g. `claimed #\d+ \(bin/claim-targets\.js, transport: [a-z-]+\)`). A two-call
`/claude-tweaks:dispatch` handoff whose first call logged the same, substantively-true event in
different prose (observed live: `2026-10-06T063143-record-2694`'s first call logged "flow: claimed
issue #2694 via MCP transport (gh CLI unavailable); tombstone reclaim from prior run..." instead
of the exact template) is denied at the second call's first push, even though the claim was real,
live, and independently verifiable against the claims-registry blob.

## Deliverables

- Loosen `hasClaimLogFor`'s (and the sibling PR-early-lifecycle check's) recognition to accept a
  claim/PR-early-lifecycle line that is semantically equivalent but not byte-exact to the
  documented template — e.g. a looser regex, or a structured marker the log line carries
  alongside its free-text prose, so a correctness-preserving round trip isn't required purely to
  satisfy the gate's string match.
- Alternatively (lower-risk, no regex loosening): document the exact-format requirement more
  prominently in `flow/claim-targets.md`'s "Log the claim (mandatory, #2492)" section, so a
  deviating log line is caught at write time rather than discovered at the next push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A claim (or PR-early-lifecycle) event logged in materially-equivalent but differently-worded
  prose by an earlier call in the same run no longer blocks a later call's first push in the same
  run, OR the write-time contract is tightened enough that this divergence cannot occur in
  practice.

## Gotchas

- Do not loosen the match so far that a genuinely missing claim (never logged at all) passes —
  the gate's whole purpose is catching exactly that case. Any looser recognition must still
  require the claimed issue number and the "claimed" semantics to be unambiguously present.

## Release Note

No user-visible change: a bookkeeping gate accepts paraphrased, but substantively equivalent, claim-log lines instead of requiring byte-exact phrasing.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md:66-73` resolves each story's `url:` against `APP_URL` before any prompt is assembled:
  - a root-relative URL is joined to `APP_URL`
  - an absolute origin that differs from `APP_URL`'s is replaced, preserving path, query and fragment
  - an origin that already matches is kept

  The step logs once per run. This was the #2283 fix (PR #2390), which changed only `story.url`.
- Step blocks are serialized verbatim into the agent prompt: `{serialize setup block as YAML}` (`:94`), `{serialize teardown block as YAML}` (`:97`) and `{serialize story.steps as YAML}` (`:100`). The qa-agent runs a `navigate` step as `playwright-cli -s=<story-id> goto <url>` (`plugin/agents/qa-agent.md:116`), so an absolute origin inside it is followed literally.
- Observed symptom (from the record): "the agent navigates to the pinned port. With several worktrees on one machine that port can belong to another session's mock, and the story's reset call clears that session's fixture state. The orchestrator has to rewrite those values by hand in every prompt."
- The story schema does not define `navigate` or name its URL field. `plugin/skills/stories/SKILL.md:35-62` lists click/fill/assert_visible only. The one shipped example writes `- action: navigate` / `target: "https://example.com/setup-page"` (`plugin/skills/stories/story-examples.md:214-215`); the record says `value`.
- Loopback hosts are already defined once for QA: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `*.localhost` (`plugin/skills/test/qa-procedures.md:107`). The same paragraph already marks stories `SKIPPED` with a reason token (`unacknowledged-remote-target`). A worktree is detected with `repoInfo(process.cwd()).isLinkedWorktree` (`plugin/skills/_shared/dev-url-detection.md:93`).

## Deliverables

1. Decision (approved in brainstorming, 2026-10-15): in `qa-prompts.md`'s URL resolution, rewrite step-level absolute origins that equal the story's own `url:` origin to `APP_URL`'s origin, using the same path/query/fragment preservation rule as `story.url`. Any other absolute loopback origin inside a step is flagged before dispatch. It is logged once per run, and on a worktree run the story is skipped, because the secondary server's port can't be assumed there. Rejected alternatives:
   - Rewrite only: it silently mis-targets a secondary server onto the app.
   - A new schema variable for secondary origins: it needs per-worktree secondary-server resolution (#3082, still open).
2. Extend the "Resolve each story's dispatch URL" block (`qa-prompts.md:66-73`) to cover every `navigate` step's URL in `setup.steps`, `story.steps` and `teardown.steps`, using the URL from `target` or `value`. Before the step blocks are serialized:
   - **Matches the story's own origin:** rewrite the origin to `APP_URL`'s. When `story.url` is root-relative, the story's own origin is `APP_URL`'s.
   - **Other loopback origin, worktree run:** mark the story `SKIPPED` with reason `unresolved-secondary-origin`, naming the origin.
   - **Other loopback origin, primary-checkout run:** dispatch unchanged and include the origin in the flag line.
   - **Non-loopback origin:** dispatch unchanged.
3. Extend the once-per-run logging (`:73`) with one rewrite-count line for step origins and one flag line listing the distinct flagged origins and the affected story ids. These go to `log-decision.js` when a run dir is active, otherwise to the QA report.
4. Document `navigate` in `stories/SKILL.md`'s Story schema (v2): `target` is its URL field (as in the shipped example). Extend the `url:`-field paragraph (`:64`) with the step-origin rule. Also align `qa-agent.md:116`'s `<url>` with the field name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new `tests/qa-prompts-step-origin.test.js` asserts that `qa-prompts.md`'s URL-resolution block:
  - names `navigate` steps in setup, steps and teardown
  - states the same-origin rewrite preserving path/query/fragment
  - states the worktree-run `SKIPPED` reason `unresolved-secondary-origin`
  - states the loopback host set or cites `qa-procedures.md`'s
- [ ] The same test asserts that `stories/SKILL.md`'s schema section documents `action: navigate` with `target`, and that `qa-agent.md`'s navigate bullet names the same field.
- [ ] Each assertion goes red when its prose is reverted.
- [ ] A worked example in `qa-prompts.md` covers a story with `url: http://127.0.0.1:9999/app`, a step `navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:9999/reset`, and a second step to `http://127.0.0.1:4010/__reset`, under `APP_URL=http://localhost:54321`. The 9999 step resolves to `http://localhost:54321/reset`, and the 4010 step is flagged (and skipped on a worktree run).
- [ ] `npm test` passes, including `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js`, which reads `qa-prompts.md`.

## Release Note

Fixed QA runs so navigation steps that point at the app's own pinned address follow the resolved app URL, and stories that would reach another local server are flagged (and skipped in worktrees) instead of touching a server the run does not own.

## Technical Approach

This change is prose only and lives in the dispatcher. The resolution happens before prompt assembly, so the templates' no-sibling-file-references contract (`qa-prompts.md:7`, restated at `:75`) is untouched, and the serialized YAML simply carries the resolved URLs. Origin comparison uses `new URL(x).origin`, matching the existing `story.url` rule. Only `navigate` steps are in scope: a `fill` value that happens to be a URL is test input and must reach the form verbatim. A skipped story's dependents follow the existing dependency rule (`qa-procedures.md:89`).

### Key Files
- `plugin/skills/test/qa-prompts.md`: URL-resolution block (`:66-73`) gains the step-origin rule, skip reason and logging; adds the worked example
- `plugin/skills/stories/SKILL.md`: schema documents `navigate` + `target`; `url:` paragraph (`:64`) gains the step rule
- `plugin/agents/qa-agent.md`: navigate bullet (`:116`) names the URL field
- `tests/qa-prompts-step-origin.test.js`: new prose conformance test

## Gotchas

- Legacy-format stories (`workflow` string, `qa-prompts.md:62`, `:156`) are free text and are not parsed. State this as a coverage limit in the block rather than silently implying total coverage.
- The `navigate` field name is undocumented today (the example uses `target`, the record says `value`). Reading both fields covers existing stories. Pin `target` as canonical going forward.
- Revisit the worktree skip when #3082 (declared `servers.yml` start command) ships secondary-server resolution. A secondary-origin variable becomes possible then.
- Related: #2283 (closed) fixed `story.url`.

## Original request

test: QA dispatch rewrites a story's url origin but not absolute origins inside navigate steps

**Summary:** The QA dispatcher resolves a story's `url:` against `APP_URL`, but an absolute origin inside a `navigate` step's `value` reaches the agent verbatim, so a story that resets a mock API on a pinned port hits whatever listens on that port.

**Kind:** Defect

**Affected component:** `/claude-tweaks:test` (`qa-prompts.md`, "Resolve each story's dispatch URL against `APP_URL`")

**Repro steps:**
1. Write a story with an absolute `url:` on one port and steps that `navigate` to a second absolute origin — for example a mock API's reset endpoint on its own fixed port — before returning to the app.
2. Run QA from a worktree whose app and mock run on other ports (the ephemeral-server path).
3. The dispatcher rewrites `url:` to `APP_URL`'s origin; the `navigate` values are serialized into the agent prompt unchanged.

**Expected vs. actual:**
Expected: a story run against a relocated app does not reach servers the run does not own — either origins inside step values are rewritten the same way `url:` is (at least the ones equal to the story's own `url:` origin), a pinned origin that differs from `APP_URL`'s is flagged before dispatch, or the story schema offers a variable for a secondary origin.
Actual: the agent navigates to the pinned port. With several worktrees on one machine that port can belong to another session's mock, and the story's reset call clears that session's fixture state. The orchestrator has to rewrite those values by hand in every prompt.

Related: #2283 fixed the same hazard for a story's `url:`; step values were not part of that fix.

**Definition:** Needed — whether to rewrite origins inside step values, or to add a secondary-origin variable to the story schema.

**Plugin version:** 6.136.0
